definition_zh: 兴趣；利益；利息；（法律上的）权益
definition_en: the state of wanting to know something; benefit or profit; money charged for borrowing
core_image: 一叠钞票上贴着一张便签，便签写着小小的数字，数字随着日期一天天变大
scene: 隔壁的张先生向银行借了一笔钱装修房子，每个月除了还本还要多付一小笔费用。The interest he pays each month looks small at first but adds up over time.
sceneCN: 这里 interest 指「借贷利息」（第 4 个义项：借款所付的额外费用）；句意为他每月支付的利息起初看似不多，但久而久之累积起来就很可观。图中可辨识物件：一叠钞票、便签上的数字、日期日历。

pos.zh: 兴趣（可数/不可数）；利益（不可数）；利息（不可数/可数）

senses.title: curiosity or attention
senses.definition: a feeling of wanting to know or learn about something
senses.definitionCN: 想要了解或学习某事的感觉
senses.example: Her interest in astronomy began in childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 她对天文学的兴趣始于童年。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, still at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，仍然居于这个词的核心。

senses.title: something attractive
senses.definition: a quality that attracts attention; a pastime
senses.definitionCN: 吸引注意力的特质；业余爱好
senses.example: Chess became his main interest after retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 退休后国际象棋成了他的主要爱好。
senses.why: The feeling turns outward and names the thing that gives the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这种感觉向外延伸，指代能带来这种感觉的事物。

senses.title: benefit or advantage
senses.definition: advantage, profit, or the wellbeing of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 优势、利润，或某人/群体的福祉
senses.example: A merger may serve the interest of both firms.
senses.exampleCN: 合并可能符合两家公司的利益。
senses.why: Interest is what matters to you, so it names what is good for you.
senses.whyCN: interest 是对你重要的东西，所以它也指代对你有利的事物。

senses.title: money charged for borrowing
senses.definition: the amount charged for borrowing money, paid on top of the principal
senses.definitionCN: 借款所收的金额，需在本金之外额外支付
senses.example: Mortgage interest rates rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年抵押贷款利率大幅上升。
senses.why: A lender has an interest in being paid back, so that interest became the fee.
senses.whyCN: 出借人在乎能否收回钱，于是这种在乎变成了费用本身。

senses.title: share or claim
senses.definition: a legal share or right in property or a firm
senses.definitionCN: 财产或企业中的合法份额或权利
senses.example: He sold his 20 percent interest in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他卖掉了自己在公司里百分之二十的权益。
senses.why: A legal claim is what you have a stake in, so interest names that stake.
senses.whyCN: 合法主张就是你有利益关系的部分，于是 interest 也指代这份 stake。

senses.title: attention by a group
senses.definition: notice or concern from the public or from authorities
senses.definitionCN: 公众或当局的注意或关注
senses.example: The new policy attracted widespread interest.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新政策引起了广泛关注。
senses.why: The word broadens from a personal feeling to a collective one.
senses.whyCN: 词义从个人感受扩展到了集体层面的关注。

senses.title: cause or side
senses.definition: a cause or movement that one supports
senses.definitionCN: 某人所支持的事业或运动
senses.example: She works in the interest of clean energy.
senses.exampleCN: 她为清洁能源事业工作。
senses.why: What you have a stake in can be an ideal, not just money.
senses.whyCN: 你有利益关系的可以是一种理想，而不只是金钱。

senses.title: legal stake
senses.definition: a legal right or claim recognised by a court
senses.definitionCN: 法院所承认的合法权利或主张
senses.example: The court will decide whose interest comes first.
senses.exampleCN: 法院将裁定谁的利益优先。
senses.why: The legal sense tightens the general sense of stake into an enforceable claim.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把一般的 stake 收紧成可执行的主张。

intro.en: Interest comes from Latin interesse, which combined 'between' and 'to be'. The 'between' sense led to 'difference', then to 'concern', 'benefit' and finally 'interest on money'.
intro.cn: interest 来自拉丁语 interesse，由「在……之间」与「是」构成。「在……之间」先引申为「差异」，再到「关心」、「利益」，最后到「利息」。

items.en: Latin interesse = inter (between) + esse (to be) meant 'to be between'; it was also used for 'it makes a difference, it matters'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 interesse = inter（在……之间）+ esse（是），意为「介于其间」，也被用来表示「有差别、有关系」。

items.en: Late Latin created a noun interestia, meaning 'difference, importance', which passed into Old French as interesse.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语造了名词 interestia，意为「差异、重要性」，传入古法语变成 interesse。

items.en: Old French interesse meant 'compensation, damages' by the twelfth century, a financial sense.
items.cn: 古法语 interesse 在 12 世纪已有「赔偿、损害赔偿金」的财务义。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the 15th century as interesse, later respelled interest to match the French past participle of 'to be'.
items.cn: 英语 15 世纪借为 interesse，后来按法语「是」的过去分词形式改拼为 interest。

items.en: The 'curiosity' sense appeared in the 17th century, then 'advantage', and the financial 'charge for borrowing' was already established in the 16th century.
items.cn: 「好奇」义出现于 17 世纪，随后是「好处」义；财务上「借款费用」在 16 世纪已确立。

items.en: Interesting comes from Old French interesser 'to concern', which shares the same Latin root interesse; both words diverged in meaning after entering English.
items.cn: interesting 来自古法语 interesser「使关心」，与 interest 同出拉丁语 interesse；两词进入英语后义分叉。

note.en: Group one holds words that look alike but come from different French or Latin stems; group two holds neighbouring financial terms.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近但来源不同的词；第二组是邻近的金融术语。

entries.definition: From interesser 'to concern'; it means 'arousing interest', not 'interest itself'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 interesser「使关心」；它指「能引起兴趣的」，而不是「兴趣」本身。

entries.definition: Feeling curiosity; shares the root but is an adjective of state.
entries.definitionCN: 感到好奇的；同根但是状态形容词。

entries.definition: Built on inter- 'between' but uses a different second element, the state.
entries.definitionCN: 由 inter-「在……之间」+ state 构成，第二成分不同。

entries.definition: From Latin intervenire 'to come between'; same inter- root, different verb stem.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 intervenire「来到其间」；同 inter- 词根，不同动词词干。

entries.definition: The percentage charged on a loan, a specific measurement of interest.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款所收的百分比，是对 interest 的计量。

entries.definition: The sum borrowed, distinct from the interest paid on top.
entries.definitionCN: 借来的本金，与额外支付的 interest 相对。

entries.definition: Any charge for a service; interest is a fee for the use of money.
entries.definitionCN: 任何服务费；interest 是用钱的费用。

entries.definition: A share of profit paid out; interest is payment for lending, dividend for owning.
entries.definitionCN: 公司利润的分红；interest 是借钱的报酬，dividend 是持股的回报。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes, real relatives, real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词、同族词和固定搭配。

normal.en: inter- means 'between' and esse means 'to be'; interest started as 'to be between, to differ'.
normal.cn: inter- 意为「在……之间」，esse 意为「是」；interest 起初是「介乎其间、有所不同」。

normal.en: The family includes interest, interesting, interested, interest-free and disinterested.
normal.cn: 同族包括 interest、interesting、interested、interest-free、disinterested。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: compound interest, vested interest, take an interest in.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：compound interest 复利、vested interest 既得利益、take an interest in 感兴趣。

normal.en: The financial sense comes from 'the difference' between what was lent and what was returned.
normal.cn: 财务义来自「借出的钱」和「还回的钱」之间的差额。

normal.en: Interesting and interest are twins from Old French interesser, 'to concern'.
normal.cn: interesting 与 interest 是同源兄弟，都来自古法语 interesser「使关心」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the extra money on one side grows every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一边堆着每月多出的那一小笔钱。

abstract.en: Picture two sides of a coin: one face is curiosity, the other is profit.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的两面：一面是好奇，一面是收益。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin merchant saying 'it makes a difference' about a loan.
abstract.cn: 想象一位古罗马商人对着贷款说「这可不一样啊」。

examples.en: Compound interest grows faster than simple interest over the years.
examples.cn: 多年下来，复利比单利增长得更快。

examples.en: She has a genuine interest in helping young researchers find grants.
examples.cn: 她真心关心帮助年轻研究者找到课题资助。

examples.en: The board acted in the interest of shareholders and depositors alike.
examples.cn: 董事会同时为股东与储户的利益行事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特瑞斯」——在你借的钱与要还的钱之间，有一份让银行在意的差额 → 利息 / 兴趣

root: 拉丁语 interesse（inter-「在……之间」+ esse「是」）→ 晚期拉丁语 interestia（差异、重要性）→ 古法语 interesse → 英语 interest。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one centre: the feeling of caring → the thing that attracts caring → benefit → money-charge → legal claim → public attention → a cause → a legally recognised stake.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个中心向外展开：在乎的感觉 → 吸引在乎的事物 → 利益 → 用钱的费用 → 法律主张 → 公众关注 → 事业 → 法律上认可的 stake。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: extra money growing on a stack of banknotes, a tiny calendar beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：钞票堆上日渐变大的那一小叠钱，旁边摆着日历。

branches.en: THE FEELING AND ITS OBJECT: curiosity itself and the thing that arouses it.
branches.cn: 感觉与对象：好奇本身，以及唤起好奇的事物。

branches.en: BENEFIT: what is good for someone becomes named as their interest.
branches.cn: 好处：对某人有利的事物就被称为他的 interest。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL FEE: a lender's care about repayment turns into a charge.
branches.cn: 财务费用：出借人对还款的在乎变成了费用。

branches.en: LEGAL STAKES: both general and formally recognised claims belong here.
branches.cn: 法律 stake：一般的和形式上认可的主张都归在这里。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND IDEAL: from public notice to a cause you support.
branches.cn: 集体与理想：从公众的关注延伸到你所支持的事业。

intro.en: Interest is built on the Latin prefix inter- and the verb esse. The English form also carried the Old French suffix -esse that became -est in some relatives.
intro.cn: interest 由拉丁语前缀 inter- 与动词 esse 构成。英语形式也带上了古法语的 -esse 后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin interesse = inter (between) + esse (to be); the noun interestia derived from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interesse = inter（在……之间）+ esse（是）；名词 interestia 由它派生。

items.example: The lender's stake sits between what is lent and what comes back.
items.exampleCN: 出借人的 stake 就介于借出的和收回的之间。

items.example: The verb carries the sense of 'making a difference, being at stake'.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词承载着「有差别、处于 stake 中」的意味。

items.structure: From Old French interesse, from Latin interestia
items.meaning: difference, concern, benefit, charge for borrowing
items.example: The word covers both emotion and finance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时覆盖感情和财务。

items.example: An interesting fact makes you stop scrolling.
items.exampleCN: 一个有趣的事实能让你停下来，不再刷屏幕。

items.example: She was interested in the lecture from the start.
items.exampleCN: 她从一开始就对这场讲座感兴趣。

items.meaning: making something do something; a present participial adjective
items.meaningCN: 使某物起作用的；现在分词形容词
items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective of effect.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表效果的形容词。

items.meaning: having received or undergone the action
items.example: Interested means 'having interest inside one'.
items.exampleCN: interested 意为「内心被 interest 击中的」。

items.example: Disinterest means 'lack of interest'.
items.exampleCN: disinterest 意为「缺乏兴趣」。

items.example: A store may offer interest-free instalments.
items.exampleCN: 商店可能提供免息分期。

items.example: The interstate highway crosses five states.
items.exampleCN: 州际公路穿过五个州。

latinEntries.meaning: to be between; to make a difference

definition_zh: 利率；借款或存款所收取/支付利息的比率
definition_en: the proportion of a loan or deposit that is charged or paid as interest, usually per year
core_image: 一条温度计，顶端是高耸的百分比数字，底端是躺在钱堆上的借款人
scene: 央行在新闻发布会上宣布将借贷成本上调，报刊头版立刻登出醒目的大字标题。The interest rate on the central bank's main facility rose by a quarter of one percent.
sceneCN: 这里 interest rate 指「央行基准利率」（第 2 个义项：中央银行向商业银行收取的利率）；句意为央行主要政策工具的利率上调了 0.25 个百分点。图中可辨识物件：新闻发布会话筒、大字标题报纸、央行徽标。

pos.zh: 利率（可数；常用复数 interest rates）

senses.title: general price of borrowing
senses.definition: the ratio of interest charged to the principal amount of a loan
senses.definitionCN: 利息与借款本金的比率
senses.example: A high interest rate makes cars and houses harder to buy.
senses.exampleCN: 高利率让汽车和房子更难买得起。
senses.why: The two parts add up: interest is the fee, rate is the proportion.
senses.whyCN: 两部分相加成义：interest 是费用，rate 是比例。

senses.title: central bank policy rate
senses.definition: the rate at which the central bank lends to commercial banks
senses.definitionCN: 中央银行向商业银行放贷所收的利率
senses.example: The Fed kept its policy rate near zero for several years.
senses.exampleCN: 美联储把政策利率维持在接近零长达数年。
senses.why: The central bank's rate sets the floor for every other rate in the economy.
senses.whyCN: 央行利率为整个经济中的其他利率定了一个底。

senses.title: deposit rate
senses.definition: the rate paid to depositors on their savings accounts
senses.definitionCN: 支付给储户的储蓄账户利率
senses.example: Depositors fled money-market funds when the deposit rate fell.
senses.exampleCN: 存款利率下降时，储户纷纷从货币市场基金撤出。
senses.why: The same phrase works for the lender side, not only the borrower side.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语既可以用在借方，也可以用在贷方。

senses.title: mortgage rate
senses.definition: the specific rate charged on home loans
senses.definitionCN: 房屋贷款所收取的特定利率
senses.example: Mortgage rates hit a ten-year high last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押贷款利率上季度创了十年新高。
senses.why: The general phrase is narrowed to the largest consumer loan category.
senses.whyCN: 通用短语被收窄到最大的消费贷款类别。

senses.title: nominal rate
senses.definition: the rate quoted before adjusting for inflation
senses.definitionCN: 扣除通胀影响之前所报的利率
senses.example: The nominal rate looked fine but the real rate turned negative.
senses.exampleCN: 名义利率看起来挺好，但实际利率变成了负的。
senses.why: The phrase attaches to the type of calculation being used.
senses.whyCN: 短语被附加到正在使用的计算方式上。

senses.title: real rate
senses.definition: the interest rate minus the rate of inflation
senses.definitionCN: 利率减去通胀率
senses.example: A negative real rate punishes savers.
senses.exampleCN: 负的实际利率会惩罚储蓄者。
senses.why: The phrase carries the context of economic measurement.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语带上了经济计量的语境。

senses.title: overnight rate
senses.definition: the rate on very short-term interbank loans, typically overnight
senses.definitionCN: 极短期银行间贷款（通常隔夜）的利率
senses.example: The overnight rate spiked when banks stopped lending to each other.
senses.exampleCN: 当银行之间不再互借，隔夜利率飙升。
senses.why: A particular term of the loan picks up the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 某种特定期限的贷款沿用了同一个短语。

senses.title: floating versus fixed
senses.definition: the rate's variability over time, a contract feature
senses.definitionCN: 利率随时间变化的方式，是合同的一个特征
senses.example: Most borrowers prefer a fixed interest rate for predictability.
senses.exampleCN: 多数借款人偏好固定利率以求可预测。
senses.why: The phrase also names a feature of how the rate behaves, not just the rate itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也命名利率行为的方式，而不只是利率本身。

intro.en: Interest rate is a compound of two old words: interest from the Latin 'to be between', and rate from the Latin 'to count'.
intro.cn: interest rate 是两个老词的复合：interest 来自拉丁语「介于其间」，rate 来自拉丁语「计数」。

items.en: Latin ratus, past participle of reri 'to count, reckon', became Old French rate, meaning 'reckoning, proportion'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ratus 是 reri「数、计算」的过去分词，变成古法语 rate，意为「计算、比例」。

items.en: Rate entered English in the 15th century meaning 'quantity measured against something else'.
items.cn: rate 于 15 世纪进入英语，指「相对于另一物所衡量的量」。

items.en: Interest had already meant the charge for borrowing by the 16th century.
items.cn: interest 到 16 世纪已指借款费用。

items.en: The fixed phrase interest rate as a term for the ratio of charge to principal appears in financial writing of the 18th century.
items.cn: 作为利息与本金比率的固定说法 interest rate 见于 18 世纪金融著作。

items.en: Later it became standard in central-bank reports and macroeconomic textbooks, often appearing in the plural.
items.cn: 后来它成为央行报告与宏观经济学教材里的标准术语，常用复数。

items.en: Source uncertain (first printed use): the earliest attestation of the compound in print has not been checked here; the Latin root reri is well established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（最早印刷用例）：此复合词的最早印刷佐证此处未查；拉丁词根 reri 则很确定。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes of rate; group two holds neighbouring terms of borrowing costs.
note.cn: 第一组是 rate 的形近词；第二组是邻近的借贷成本术语。

entries.definition: Meaning 'proportion, speed, level'; interest rate uses it in the 'proportion' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「比例、速度、水平」；interest rate 用的是「比例」义。

entries.definition: An assessment of quality or creditworthiness, not a proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或信用的评估，不是比例。

entries.definition: Any quotient of two numbers; interest rate is a specific ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 任意两个数的比值；interest rate 是一种特定的 ratio。

entries.definition: Speed of movement or change; rate covers both proportion and speed.
entries.definitionCN: 移动或变化的速度；rate 同时覆盖比例和速度。

entries.definition: The money charged, not the proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 被收取的钱本身，不是比例。

entries.definition: A rate that also includes some fees, broader than pure interest rate.
entries.definitionCN: 还包含部分手续费，比纯 interest rate 更宽。

entries.definition: The return earned, often per year, on an investment; rate is the price charged for borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 投资每年的回报；rate 是借款所收的价格。

entries.definition: The rate at which the Fed lends directly to banks, narrower than the general phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 美联储直接向银行放贷的利率，比这个短语更具体。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: interest = the fee; rate = a proportion; together they give the fee as a proportion of the loan.
normal.cn: interest 是费用，rate 是比例；合起来就是费用占贷款的比例。

normal.en: rate comes from Latin ratus 'reckoned', same root as ratio.
normal.cn: rate 来自拉丁语 ratus「已计算的」，与 ratio 同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: raise the interest rate, cut the interest rate, fixed interest rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：raise the interest rate 加息、cut 降息、fixed 固定利率。

normal.en: The Fed, the ECB and the PBOC all publish interest rate decisions.
normal.cn: 美联储、欧央行、中国央行都会公布利率决议。

normal.en: Nominal rate is before inflation; real rate is after inflation.
normal.cn: 名义利率是通胀前的，实际利率是通胀后的。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer where the mercury is a percent sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一根温度计，水银柱是一个百分号。

abstract.en: Picture two lanes: one for borrowers (it hurts when high), one for savers (it helps when high).
abstract.cn: 想象两条车道：借款人那条高了就痛，储蓄者那条高了就乐。

abstract.en: Picture a central banker announcing a number to flashing cameras.
abstract.cn: 想象央行行长在一片闪光灯中宣布一个数字。

examples.en: A falling interest rate encouraged firms to borrow for new equipment.
examples.cn: 利率下降鼓励企业借钱购买新设备。

examples.en: Savers moved their money when the bank cut its deposit interest rate.
examples.cn: 银行下调存款利率后，储户把钱转走了。

examples.en: Mortgages became unaffordable when the average interest rate reached seven percent.
examples.cn: 当平均利率达到百分之七时，房贷变得负担不起。

dict_mnemonic.text: interest + rate = 借款的费用比例 → 利率

root: interest（拉丁语 interesse）+ rate（拉丁语 ratus「已计算的」，过去分词）。短语见于 18 世纪金融文献。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses progress from the general price of borrowing → the central bank's policy tool → deposit side → mortgage → nominal versus real → very short term → contract feature.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般借贷价格→央行政策工具→存款端→抵押贷款→名义与实际→极短期→合同特征，依次展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer with a percent sign for mercury, beside a stack of banknotes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根水银柱是百分号的温度计，旁边堆着钞票。

branches.en: THE GENERAL PRICE: a proportion that sits on every loan.
branches.cn: 一般价格：附着在每笔贷款上的比例。

branches.en: POLICY AND DEPOSIT: the two main institutional uses, central bank and depository.
branches.cn: 政策与存款：两种主要制度性用法，央行与存款机构。

branches.en: THE BIGGEST CONSUMER LOAN: mortgages carry the headline rate people notice most.
branches.cn: 最大宗消费贷款：房贷上的利率最受普通人关注。

branches.en: ECONOMIC MEASUREMENT: nominal and real differ in whether inflation is subtracted.
branches.cn: 经济计量：名义与实际的差别在于是否扣除了通胀。

branches.en: SHORT TERM AND CONTRACT: overnight loans and the fixed-or-variable choice in a contract.
branches.cn: 短期与合同：隔夜贷款，以及合同中固定还是浮动的选择。

intro.en: Interest rate is a compound of two free morphemes; rate itself is a Latin past-participial borrowing.
intro.cn: interest rate 是两个自由语素的复合；rate 本身是借自拉丁语过去分词的词。

latinIntro.en: Rate comes from Latin ratus, past participle of reri 'to count, reckon'.
latinIntro.cn: rate 来自拉丁语 ratus，是 reri「数、计算」的过去分词。

items.example: Interest is what the borrower pays above the principal.
items.exampleCN: interest 是借款人在本金之外还要付的部分。

items.example: Rate tells you how much of the principal goes to interest.
items.exampleCN: rate 告诉你本金中有多少比例变成 interest。

items.example: The rate is a reckoned proportion.
items.exampleCN: rate 是算出来的比例。

items.example: Interest rate is a ratio of interest to principal.
items.exampleCN: 利率是利息与本金之比。

items.meaning: a classification by quality or credit
items.meaningCN: 按质量或信用分出的等级
items.example: A poor credit rating raises the interest rate.
items.exampleCN: 信用等级差会抬高利率。

items.example: Rating is the result of applying a rate to something.
items.exampleCN: rating 是把 rate 用于某物后的结果。

items.example: A fixed rate does not change over the loan.
items.exampleCN: 固定利率在贷款期内不变。

items.example: A variable rate tracks a market index.
items.exampleCN: 浮动利率跟随某个市场指数波动。

items.example: The annual interest rate is the standard measure.
items.exampleCN: 年利率是标准的计量方式。

items.example: The overnight rate spikes in panics.
items.exampleCN: 恐慌时隔夜利率会飙升。

definition_zh: 本金；主要的；校长；委托人
definition_en: the original sum of money borrowed; main or most important; a head teacher; one who authorises an agent
core_image: 一棵树干粗壮的大树，旁边摆着几张钞票，树上挂着写着小百分比的牌子
scene: 小李买房时向银行贷了一笔钱，还款表里第一项是本金，另一项是额外的费用。He paid off the principal of his mortgage ten years early.
sceneCN: 这里 principal 指「贷款本金」（第 3 个义项：借款的原始金额）；句意为他提前十年还清了房贷的本金。图中可辨识物件：还款表格、树干代表的 principal、挂着的小牌子代表利息。

pos.zh: 主要的；最重要的
本金；校长；委托人

senses.title: main or primary
senses.definition: first in importance or rank
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性或地位上居于首位的
senses.example: The principal cause of the fire was faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾的主要原因是电线老化。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, direct from the Latin 'first, chief'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，直接来自拉丁语「第一、首要」。

senses.title: head of a school
senses.definition: the head teacher of a school
senses.definitionCN: 一所学校的校长
senses.example: The principal gave a speech at graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表讲话。
senses.why: The head of an institution inherits the 'first, chief' sense.
senses.whyCN: 机构的负责人承接了「第一、首要」的意思。

senses.title: original sum lent
senses.definition: the amount of money originally borrowed, before interest is added
senses.definitionCN: 最初借来的金额，在加上利息之前
senses.example: Each monthly payment covers both principal and interest.
senses.exampleCN: 每月的还款既包括本金也包括利息。
senses.why: The original sum is the main part of the debt, separate from the interest that builds on it.
senses.whyCN: 原始金额是债务的主要部分，与在它之上累积的利息分开。

senses.title: party to a deal
senses.definition: a person for whom an agent acts in business or law
senses.definitionCN: 在商业或法律事务中由代理人代为行动的人
senses.example: As principal, she authorised her lawyer to sign the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 作为委托人，她授权律师代自己签合同。
senses.why: The one who authorises is the chief actor behind the agent.
senses.whyCN: 授权者是代理人背后的首要行为人。

senses.title: head of an embassy
senses.definition: the main diplomatic representative below an ambassador
senses.definitionCN: 低于大使级别的主要外交代表
senses.example: The embassy's principal met the foreign minister.
senses.exampleCN: 大使馆一等秘书拜会了外长。
senses.why: Another institutional 'first in rank' sense.
senses.whyCN: 另一种制度性的「首位」义。

senses.title: capital invested
senses.definition: money invested, as distinct from the income it produces
senses.definitionCN: 已投资的钱，与它产生的收益相区别
senses.example: The fund's principal remained intact through the downturn.
senses.exampleCN: 在衰退期间，基金的本金保持完好。
senses.why: The sum that sits underneath any return is the principal.
senses.whyCN: 任何收益之下的那笔钱就是 principal。

senses.title: main performer
senses.definition: the leading performer in a ballet, opera or similar
senses.definitionCN: 芭蕾、歌剧等中的主要演员
senses.example: The principal dancer fell ill before the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 主演在开演前病倒了。
senses.why: Again the 'chief, first' sense applied to cast ranking.
senses.whyCN: 又是「首要、第一」义应用到演员排序上。

senses.title: main road
senses.definition: a main road, especially in the town or the principal artery
senses.definitionCN: 一条主要道路，尤指城镇里的主干道
senses.example: The principal road was closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 那条主干道因维修封闭。
senses.why: A road that carries most traffic is the chief one.
senses.whyCN: 承载最多车流的路就是主干道。

intro.en: Principal and principle both descend from Latin princeps, but they split in meaning. Principal kept 'first in rank', principle took 'a rule'.
intro.cn: principal 与 principle 都来自拉丁语 princeps，但义分叉了。principal 保持「地位第一」，principle 则指「一条规则」。

items.en: Latin princeps meant 'first, chief'; it was built from primus 'first' + capere 'to take'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 意为「第一的、首要的」，由 primus「第一」+ capere「拿、取」构成。

items.en: Old French principal meant 'first' in the 12th century and passed into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 principal 在 12 世纪意为「第一的」，传入中古英语。

items.en: By the 14th century English principal meant 'chief person, head of a school', and by the 16th century the financial 'sum lent' appeared.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪英语 principal 已指「首要人物、校长」，到 16 世纪出现财务上「借出的金额」义。

items.en: Principle came through Latin principium 'beginning, rule'; it recorded the 'rule' sense that principal did not keep.
items.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium「起点、规则」，它承接了 principal 没有保持的「规则」义。

items.en: By the 19th century principal and interest became standard paired terms in loan documents.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，principal 与 interest 成为贷款文书里的固定配对术语。

items.en: Source solid: primus and capere are well documented. The split between principal and principle is a long-standing folk-etymology trap in English.
items.cn: 来源可靠：primus 与 capere 均有充分文献。principal 与 principle 的区分长期是英语使用者的陷阱。

note.en: Look-alikes are words with similar spelling; near meanings share the 'chief' or 'investment' territory.
note.cn: 形近是拼写相近的词；近义是与「首要」或「投资本金」领域邻近的词。

entries.definition: A basic truth or rule; not a person or a sum of money.
entries.definitionCN: 基本原则或规则；不指人也不指钱。

entries.definition: A male royal; shares the princeps root directly.
entries.definitionCN: 男性王室；直接共享 princeps 词根。

entries.definition: A female royal; from prince, same root but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 女性王室；来自 prince，同根但不相同。

entries.definition: The word is spelt -pal for the person and the money, -ple for the rule.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词本身：指人和钱时拼 -pal，指规则是 principle 拼 -ple。

entries.tag: the fee that sits on principal
entries.definition: The money paid in addition to the principal on a loan.
entries.definitionCN: 在 principal 之上额外支付的钱。

entries.definition: Money used to generate income; broader than principal, which is the amount of a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 用来产生收益的钱；比 principal 宽，principal 特指债务的金额。

entries.definition: A chief person; principal is more formal for the role.
entries.definitionCN: 主要人物；principal 用于这个角色更正式。

entries.definition: A governing principle, but 'rule' is narrower than 'principle' (which is spelled -ple).
entries.definitionCN: 一条规则；但 rule 比 principle（拼 -ple 的那个）更窄。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes, real relatives, real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词、同族词和固定搭配。

normal.en: principal = princeps root; 'the first, chief' sense is still there.
normal.cn: principal 的根是 princeps，「第一、首要」义一直存在。

normal.en: principal (person, money) vs principle (rule): -pal is for people and principal has -al adjective ending.
normal.cn: principal（指人、钱）与 principle（指规则）：-pal 对应 person，principal 里有 -al 形容词后缀。

normal.en: Fixed pairs: principal and interest.
normal.cn: 固定配对：principal and interest。

normal.en: primus 'first' is shared with prime, primary, primitive.
normal.cn: primus「第一」还共享于 prime、primary、primitive。

normal.en: capere 'to take' is shared with capture, captive, capability.
normal.cn: capere「拿」还共享于 capture、captive、capability。

abstract.en: Picture a trunk and branches: the trunk is principal, branches are interest.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树：树干是 principal，树枝是 interest。

abstract.en: Picture a school assembly where the principal stands at the front.
abstract.cn: 想象全校集会，校长站在最前面。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin nobleman saying 'I am first'.
abstract.cn: 想象一位拉丁语贵族说「我是第一」。

examples.en: Make extra payments to reduce the principal faster on your mortgage.
examples.cn: 额外还款可以更快地减少房贷的本金。

examples.en: The principal investigator led the team through three years of fieldwork.
examples.cn: 首席研究员带领团队完成了三年的实地工作。

examples.en: The principal's main objection was that the plan ignored local concerns.
examples.cn: 主要反对理由是该计划忽略了当地关切。

dict_mnemonic.text: -pal 代表人/钱（Principal），-ple 代表规则（Principle）

root: 拉丁语 princeps（primus「第一」+ capere「拿、取」）→ 古法语 principal → 英语 principal；与 principle（来自 principium「起点」）同源但义分叉。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from 'first, chief' → main → head of institution → sum lent (the chief part of a debt) → one behind an agent → embassy chief → investment capital → main performer → main road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「第一、首要」向外辐射：主要的 → 机构负责人 → 借出的金额（债务的首要部分）→ 代理人背后的人 → 使馆主要官员 → 投资本金 → 主要演员 → 主要道路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree trunk labelled PRINCIPAL with thin interest branches growing from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根树干贴着 PRINCIPAL 标签，上面长着细小的 interest 树枝。

branches.en: THE CORE ADJECTIVE: chief, main, first in importance.
branches.cn: 核心形容词：首要的、主要的、第一的。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL HEADS AND MAIN THINGS: school, embassy, stage, road.
branches.cn: 机构负责人与主要事物：学校、使馆、舞台、道路。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL CORE: the sum lent, separate from interest.
branches.cn: 财务核心：借出的金额，与 interest 相区分。

branches.en: INVESTMENT USE: capital invested, not income.
branches.cn: 投资用法：投入的本金，不是收益。

branches.en: THE LEGAL ACTOR: the one authorising an agent.
branches.cn: 法律行为者：授权代理人的那一方。

intro.en: Principal comes from Latin princeps, built from primus 'first' and capere 'to take'. The suffix -al was added in French.
intro.cn: principal 来自拉丁语 princeps，由 primus「第一」和 capere「拿」构成。-al 后缀是后来加的。

latinIntro.en: Latin princeps (from primus + capere) is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 princeps（primus + capere）是直接来源。

items.example: The principal is the first, chief part.
items.exampleCN: principal 是首要的那部分。

items.example: Princeps was 'one who takes the first place'.
items.exampleCN: Princeps 意为「占据第一位的人」。

items.example: The Roman Senate called Augustus princeps.
items.exampleCN: 罗马元老院称奥古斯都为 princeps。

items.example: French added -al to princeps to make the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 法语给 princeps 加了 -al 变成形容词。

items.example: The principal dancer in Swan Lake is sometimes called the princess.
items.exampleCN: 《天鹅湖》的主演有时被称作公主。

items.example: The region is principally agricultural.
items.exampleCN: 该地区主要以农业为主。

items.example: He offered a princely sum for the old boat.
items.exampleCN: 他为那艘旧船开了个相当可观的价。

items.example: Prime real estate is any principal location.
items.exampleCN: 优质地段就是 principal 的位置。

items.example: Primary education is the principal foundation.
items.exampleCN: 小学教育是 principal 的基础。

items.example: The capere root also appears in 'capture' and 'capable'.
items.exampleCN: capere 词根还出现在 capture 和 capable 里。

definition_en: a loan secured against a property; to give property as security for a debt
core_image: 一所房子，它的地基被一根粗粗的锁链拴在银行大楼上
scene: 年轻人刚领到第一张工资单，银行顾问就在桌上摊开了一份写满数字的长合同。They took out a mortgage to buy their first apartment.
sceneCN: 这里 mortgage 指「抵押贷款」（第 1 个义项：以房产为担保的借款）；句意为他们通过按揭贷款买了第一套公寓。图中可辨识物件：房屋平面图、银行合同、工资单。

pos.zh: 抵押贷款（可数）
以……作抵押

derivatives.zh: 出借抵押贷款的人/机构

senses.title: loan secured on property
senses.definition: a long-term loan for which the borrower's property serves as security
senses.definitionCN: 以借款人的房产作为担保的长期贷款
senses.example: Most people need a mortgage to buy a home.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人买房需要按揭。
senses.why: The house pledges its value until the debt dies, matching the etymology.
senses.whyCN: 房子把自己的价值押上去，直到债务消失，正好对应词源。

senses.title: the act of securing
senses.definition: the legal act of giving property as security for a debt
senses.definitionCN: 以财产为债务作担保的法律行为
senses.example: The mortgage was recorded at the county registry.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押登记被记入县登记处。
senses.why: The noun of the act follows from the loan it creates.
senses.whyCN: 行为的名词义从它所产生的贷款衍生而来。

senses.title: to pledge property
senses.definition: to give property as security for a loan
senses.definitionCN: 把财产押出去作贷款的担保
senses.example: They mortgaged their cottage to fund the business.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把小木屋抵押出去以资助生意。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb by a usual shift.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，是常见的词类转换。

senses.title: a particular loan product
senses.definition: a specific mortgage arrangement such as fixed-rate, variable, or balloon
senses.definitionCN: 固定利率、浮动、气球贷等具体安排
senses.example: An adjustable-rate mortgage suited their short stay.
senses.exampleCN: 可调整利率的 mortgage 适合他们短期居住的需求。
senses.why: The general term names one design of the same contract.
senses.whyCN: 通用术语被用来指同一种合同的某种设计。

senses.title: debt burden, figuratively
senses.definition: a heavy or long-lasting financial burden
senses.definitionCN: 沉重或长期的财务负担
senses.example: His student loan feels like a mortgage on his future.
senses.exampleCN: 他的助学贷款就像给未来押了一份按揭。
senses.why: A lasting debt mirrors the long-term house loan.
senses.whyCN: 一笔长期债务和长期房贷在形状上相似。

senses.title: commercial property loan
senses.definition: a loan secured against a non-residential building or land
senses.definitionCN: 以非住宅建筑或土地为担保的贷款
senses.example: The developer used a commercial mortgage for the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 开发商用商业抵押贷款建起了那座塔楼。
senses.why: The same legal tool serves business property too.
senses.whyCN: 同一种法律工具也适用于商业物业。

senses.title: the security instrument
senses.definition: the legal document that sets out the pledge of property
senses.definitionCN: 规定财产抵押的法律文件
senses.example: The mortgage had to be signed by both spouses.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押契据必须由夫妻双方签字。
senses.why: The act creates the paper that records it.
senses.whyCN: 行为产生了记录它的那张纸。

senses.title: death pledge, literal etymology
senses.definition: a pledge that dies when the debt is repaid
senses.definitionCN: 当债务还清时即终止的质押
senses.example: The etymology points to mortgage = mort (dead) + gage (pledge).
senses.exampleCN: 词源指出 mortgage = mort（死）+ gage（誓约）。
senses.why: The etymology re-surfaces as a learnt sense.
senses.whyCN: 词源学把它重新作为一个学术义项提出来。

intro.en: Mortgage literally means 'death pledge'. It comes from Old French mort 'dead' and gage 'pledge', because the pledge dies when the debt is repaid.
intro.cn: Mortgage 字面上就是「死誓」。来自古法语 mort「死」与 gage「誓约、抵押」，因为债务还清后这份质押就「死了」。

items.en: Old French mort meant 'dead'; it comes from Latin mors 'death'.
items.cn: 古法语 mort 意为「死的」，来自拉丁语 mors「死亡」。

items.en: Old French gage meant 'pledge, warranty'; it came from Frankish *wagjo 'pledge'.
items.cn: 古法语 gage 意为「誓约、担保」，来自法兰克语 *wagjo「抵押」。

items.en: Old French mortgage was used in law by the 12th century for a pledge that ends (dies) when the debt is settled.
items.cn: 古法语 mortgage 在 12 世纪已用于法律，指债务清偿后即终止的质押。

items.en: The word entered English through the Normans in the 14th century, spelled morgage at first.
items.cn: 诺曼人把这个词带入英语，14 世纪刚进入时拼作 morgage。

items.en: By the 20th century it became the standard term for home loan; subprime mortgage appeared in the 1990s.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪它成为房贷的标准说法；subprime mortgage 次级按揭在 1990 年代出现。

items.en: Solid etymology: mort and gage are both well attested. The Frankish *wagjo is a reconstructed root but widely accepted.
items.cn: 词源可靠：mort 与 gage 均有充分佐证。法兰克语 *wagjo 为构拟形式但被广泛接受。

note.en: Look-alikes share the -gage ending; near meanings are neighbouring ways to borrow against property.
note.cn: 形近是共用 -gage 结尾的词；近义是邻近的以财产借贷的方式。

entries.definition: From French gantelet 'little glove'; not from mortgage at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 gantelet「小手套」；与 mortgage 无关。

entries.definition: A regular payment for work; shares the *wagjo root of gage 'pledge'.
entries.definitionCN: 工资；与 gage 同出法兰克语 *wagjo。

entries.definition: To measure or a measurement; possibly related to gage 'pledge' through notion of 'guaranteed measurement'.
entries.definitionCN: 测量或量具；可能通过「确定的度量」与 gage 相连。

entries.definition: To humiliate; from Latin mors 'death' + facere 'make'.
entries.definitionCN: 羞辱；来自 mors「死」+ facere「制造」。

entries.definition: Property pledged for a loan; mortgage is the loan itself secured by it.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款质押的财产；mortgage 是以它作担保的贷款。

entries.definition: Any borrowing; mortgage is a specific long-term property-secured loan.
entries.definitionCN: 任何借款；mortgage 是特定的长期房产担保借款。

entries.definition: A US alternative to mortgage where a trustee holds the property.
entries.definitionCN: 美国替代 mortgage 的形式，由受托人持有物业。

entries.definition: A loan against the equity in your house, a kind of second mortgage.
entries.definitionCN: 以房屋净值为抵押的贷款，是 second mortgage 的一种。

normal.en: mort (dead) + gage (pledge) = death pledge; the pledge dies when the debt dies.
normal.cn: mort（死）+ gage（誓约）= 死誓；债没了，誓也没了。

normal.en: mort is the same root as mortal, mortify, immortal.
normal.cn: mort 与 mortal、mortify、immortal 同根。

normal.en: gage is the same root as wage (a pledge for your work).
normal.cn: gage 与 wage（以工作换抵押）同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take out a mortgage, pay off a mortgage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：take out a mortgage 申请按揭、pay off 还清。

normal.en: Subprime mortgage became infamous in 2008.
normal.cn: 2008 年 subprime mortgage 臭名远扬。

abstract.en: Picture a house with a little tombstone in front of it that disappears when the debt is paid.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子前面有块小墓碑，还清债务时墓碑就消失了。

abstract.en: Picture a couple signing their lives away at a mortgage broker's desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一对情侣在按揭经纪人的桌上签下自己的人生。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin-speaking banker saying 'this pledge will die with the debt'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个会说拉丁语的银行家说「这份誓约会随债一同死掉」。

examples.en: A jump in mortgage rates sent the housing market into a slump.
examples.cn: 按揭利率一跳高，房地产市场就陷入低迷。

examples.en: They mortgaged the family farm to pay for their daughter's cancer treatment.
examples.cn: 他们把家族农场抵押出去，为女儿的癌症治疗筹钱。

examples.en: Many homeowners found themselves underwater when their mortgage exceeded the house value.
examples.cn: 许多房主发现自己的负债超过了房屋价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: mort（死）+ gage（誓约）= 死誓 → 债务清时誓约亡 → 按揭

root: 古法语 mort（拉丁语 mors「死亡」）+ gage（法兰克语 *wagjo「誓约」）。债务还清后质押即「死亡」，故名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from the loan itself → the act → the verb → a type → figurative burden → commercial property → the document → the etymological 'death pledge'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从贷款本身 → 行为 → 动词 → 某一类型 → 比喻的负担 → 商业物业 → 合同文书 → 词源学上的「死誓」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house tied to a bank by a thick chain, with a tiny tombstone beside the chain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座房子用粗粗的链条拴在银行上，链条旁有一块小墓碑。

branches.en: THE HOME LOAN: the most common use people know.
branches.cn: 房贷：普通人最熟悉的用法。

branches.en: THE LEGAL ACT AND VERB: what you do and the act itself.
branches.cn: 法律行为与动词：你做的事和行为本身。

branches.en: SPECIFIC DESIGNS: fixed-rate, variable, balloon.
branches.cn: 具体设计：固定、浮动、气球贷。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE BURDEN: a lasting debt on your future.
branches.cn: 比喻负担：压在未来身上的长期债。

branches.en: BUSINESS, PAPER, ETYMOLOGY: commercial use, the document, and the literal 'death pledge'.
branches.cn: 商业、文书、词源：商用、合同文书、字面义的「死誓」。

intro.en: Mortgage is a compound of Old French mort 'dead' and gage 'pledge'.
intro.cn: mortgage 是古法语 mort（死）+ gage（誓约）的复合。

latinIntro.en: Mort comes from Latin mors 'death'; gage comes from Frankish *wagjo.
latinIntro.cn: mort 来自拉丁语 mors「死」；gage 来自法兰克语 *wagjo。

items.structure: Old French mort, from Latin mors
items.example: The pledge dies when the debt dies.
items.exampleCN: 债没了，誓也就没了。

items.example: Wages come from the same Frankish root.
items.exampleCN: wage 工资也来自同一个法兰克语词根。

items.meaning: a pledge that dies; a house loan
items.example: Every mortgage is a death pledge in the original sense.
items.exampleCN: 每一笔 mortgage 按字源都是一个死誓。

items.example: The mortgagor keeps living in the house.
items.exampleCN: 抵押人仍住在房子里。

items.meaning: the lender who receives the pledge
items.example: The mortgagee can foreclose if payments stop.
items.exampleCN: 如果停止还款，抵押权人可以没收房屋。

items.example: Mortgage shares the mort root with mortal.
items.exampleCN: mortgage 与 mortal 共享 mort 词根。

items.example: Mortgage is the opposite of immortal in one sense.
items.exampleCN: mortgage 在某个意义上与 immortal 相反。

items.example: The mort root carries 'death' through English.
items.exampleCN: mort 词根带着「死」贯穿英语。

items.example: A wage is what you pledge your work for.
items.exampleCN: wage 就是你以工作作质押所换的东西。

items.example: The mortgagee receives the pledge.
items.exampleCN: mortgagee 是接受质押的那一方。

definition_zh: 抵押物；抵押品；附带的；并行的
definition_en: property pledged as security for a debt; running side by side, parallel
core_image: 一个保险箱里塞满了金条和房产证，保险箱的钥匙挂在银行的门框上
scene: 一位创业者拿着一份专利申请走进银行，希望用它做担保换一笔启动资金。The bank accepted the patent as collateral for the loan.
sceneCN: 这里 collateral 指「贷款抵押品」（第 3 个义项：为债务担保而抵押的财产）；句意为银行接受了这项专利作为贷款的抵押品。图中可辨识物件：专利证书、贷款合同、保险箱。

pos.zh: 抵押品（不可数；可数时指多项）
并行的；附带的；侧面的

senses.title: side by side
senses.definition: running along the side of something; parallel
senses.definitionCN: 沿着某物的一侧延伸的；平行的
senses.example: A collateral vein runs beside the main river.
senses.exampleCN: 一条并行的支流沿着主河道流淌。
senses.why: The root means 'side', so the first sense is literal position.
senses.whyCN: 词根的意思是「侧面」，所以第一个义项是字面位置。

senses.title: accompanying, secondary
senses.definition: accompanying but secondary to something else
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着但居次要地位的
senses.example: Collateral benefits came from the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 合并带来了附带利益。
senses.why: What sits beside something is secondary to the main thing.
senses.whyCN: 坐在旁边的东西是主要事物的次要伴随物。

senses.title: security for a debt
senses.definition: property pledged to guarantee repayment of a loan
senses.definitionCN: 为保证贷款偿还而质押的财产
senses.example: Start-ups often lack collateral for bank loans.
senses.exampleCN: 初创公司往往没有抵押品来申请银行贷款。
senses.why: This is the financial borrowing of the 'sitting beside' idea: property sits beside the loan as its guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 这是金融上对「坐旁边」想法的借用：财产坐在贷款旁边作担保。

senses.title: side issue
senses.definition: a matter accompanying but separate from the main issue
senses.definitionCN: 伴随但独立于主要问题的一件事
senses.example: Collateral questions delayed the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 一些次要问题延迟了听证。
senses.why: Another extension of 'sitting beside' the main thing.
senses.whyCN: 另一种「坐在主要事物旁边」的延伸。

senses.title: cross-connected vessels
senses.definition: connected through side paths, especially of blood vessels
senses.definitionCN: 通过侧支连接的，尤指血管
senses.example: Collateral vessels supplied blood around the blockage.
senses.exampleCN: 侧支血管绕开堵塞为组织供血。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the 'side' sense for vessels that run beside the main path.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用「侧面」义来指沿着主要通路旁边走的血管。

senses.title: collateral damage
senses.definition: harm to bystanders from a military or political action
senses.definitionCN: 军事或政治行动中给旁观者造成的伤害
senses.example: Strikes risk heavy collateral damage in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤城市空袭可能造成严重附带损害。
senses.why: The damage sits beside the intended target.
senses.whyCN: 这种损害发生在瞄准目标的旁边。

senses.title: additional evidence
senses.definition: evidence that supports but does not directly prove
senses.definitionCN: 能支持但不能直接证明的证据
senses.example: The letter provided collateral for the witness's claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信为证人的主张提供了旁证。
senses.why: Evidence that sits beside the main case.
senses.whyCN: 坐在主要案件旁边的证据。

senses.title: network of backups
senses.definition: interconnected backup channels in a network
senses.definitionCN: 网络中互相连接的备用通道
senses.example: The internet relies on collateral links to survive outages.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网靠备用链路挺过中断。
senses.why: Side channels that run beside the main ones.
senses.whyCN: 沿着主通道旁边走的侧面通道。

intro.en: Collateral comes from Latin lateralis 'of the side', with col- 'together' added. Literally 'alongside'.
intro.cn: collateral 来自拉丁语 lateralis「侧面的」，前面加了 col-「一起」。字面意思是「沿旁边走」。

items.en: Latin latus 'side, flank' gave lateralis 'of the side'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 latus「侧面、胁部」产生 lateralis「侧面的」。

items.en: The prefix col- (a form of com- 'together') was added, making collateralis 'running alongside'.
items.cn: 加上前缀 col-（com-「一起」的一种形式），变成 collateralis「沿旁边一起走的」。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the 15th century meaning 'side by side, parallel'.
items.cn: 这个形容词于 15 世纪进入英语，意为「并排的、平行的」。

items.en: The financial noun meaning 'security for a loan' appeared in legal writing by the 17th century.
items.cn: 财务名词义「贷款担保」见于 17 世纪法律文书。

items.en: The phrase collateral damage emerged in military jargon around the 1950s and broadened after 2001.
items.cn: collateral damage 这个说法 1950 年代见于军队术语，2001 年后被广泛使用。

items.en: Latin roots are solid: latus, lateralis, com- are all well attested.
items.cn: 拉丁词根来源可靠：latus、lateralis、com- 均有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the lateralis root; near meanings sit around loan security.
note.cn: 形近共享 lateralis 词根；近义围绕贷款担保展开。

entries.definition: Of or relating to the side; collateral carries the same root with col- added.
entries.definitionCN: 侧面的；collateral 是这个词根加上 col-。

entries.definition: Between two sides or countries; same lateralis root.
entries.definitionCN: 双边的；同 lateralis 词根。

entries.definition: One-sided; same lateralis root.
entries.definitionCN: 单边的；同 lateralis 词根。

entries.definition: Having equal sides, as a triangle; same root.
entries.definitionCN: 等边的；同根。

entries.definition: A loan backed by collateral; collateral is what backs it.
entries.definitionCN: 以 collateral 作担保的贷款；collateral 是担保的东西。

entries.definition: A promise to repay; collateral is actual property pledged, not just a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 保证付款的承诺；collateral 是实际押出去的财产，不只是承诺。

entries.definition: Can mean a pledge, a financial asset, or safety; narrower than collateral in some uses.
entries.definitionCN: 可以指质押、金融资产或安全；某些用法比 collateral 更宽。

entries.definition: An initial lump sum; not security, but a partial commitment of value.
entries.definitionCN: 首付款；不是担保，而是价值的部分投入。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: col- 'together' + lateralis 'of the side' = running alongside.
normal.cn: col-「一起」+ lateralis「侧面的」= 沿旁边走。

normal.en: latus 'side' is shared with lateral, bilateral, unilateral, equilateral.
normal.cn: latus「侧面」与 lateral、bilateral、unilateral、equilateral 同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: collateral damage, collateral evidence, put up collateral.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：collateral damage 附带损害、collateral evidence 旁证、put up collateral 提供抵押。

normal.en: The financial sense is property that sits alongside the loan.
normal.cn: 财务义就是坐在贷款旁边的财产。

normal.en: In medicine, collateral vessels run beside the main artery.
normal.cn: 医学里 collateral 血管沿主动脉旁边走。

abstract.en: Picture a row of houses beside a river with one house pledged to the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象河边一排房子，其中一栋被押给了银行。

abstract.en: Picture two parallel lines: one is the loan, the other is the collateral.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线：一条是贷款，一条是抵押品。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier aiming at a target while a bystander stands in the collateral line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个士兵瞄准目标，一个旁观者站在 collateral 线上。

examples.en: Small businesses struggled because banks demanded more collateral than they owned.
examples.cn: 小企业日子不好过，因为银行要求的抵押品比他们拥有的还多。

examples.en: The military said it did not expect significant collateral damage from the raid.
examples.cn: 军方表示预计这次突袭不会造成重大附带损害。

examples.en: Doctors opened a blocked artery with the help of collateral vessels that had grown around it.
examples.cn: 医生借助在堵塞动脉周围长出的侧支血管疏通了它。

dict_mnemonic.text: col-（一起）+ lateral（侧面）= 并排、附带 → 贷款旁边并排摆的东西 → 抵押品

root: 拉丁语 latus「侧面」→ lateralis「侧面的」→ 加前缀 col-（com- 的变体）→ collateralis「沿旁边走的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend from literal 'side by side' → accompanying/secondary → pledged property (financial borrowing of 'sitting beside') → side issue → medicine (side vessels) → bystander harm → supporting evidence → network backups.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面「并排」→ 伴随/次要 → 质押财产（财务上借「坐旁边」的想法）→ 次要问题 → 医学（侧支血管）→ 旁观者所受损害 → 旁证 → 网络备份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two parallel lines, one the loan, one the property pledged beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条平行线，一条是贷款，一条是押在旁边的财产。

branches.en: THE LITERAL SIDE: running along the side of something.
branches.cn: 字面的「侧面」：沿着某物旁边走。

branches.en: SECONDARY THINGS: accompanying benefits or side issues.
branches.cn: 次要的事物：附带利益或次要问题。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL USE: property that sits beside the loan.
branches.cn: 财务用法：坐在贷款旁边的财产。

branches.en: MEDICAL SIDE VESSELS: blood vessels running beside the main path.
branches.cn: 医学侧支血管：沿主通路旁边走的血管。

branches.en: WIDER FIGURATIVE USES: bystander harm, supporting evidence, network backups.
branches.cn: 更宽的比喻用法：旁观者受害、旁证、网络备份。

intro.en: Collateral builds on lateralis, itself from latus 'side', with col- as the 'together' prefix.
intro.cn: collateral 建立在 lateralis 之上，lateralis 来自 latus「侧面」，col- 是「一起」的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus 'side' → lateralis → collateralis with col-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latus「侧面」→ lateralis → 加 col- 变成 collateralis。

items.example: The word is rooted in 'side'.
items.exampleCN: 这个词扎根于「侧面」。

items.meaning: of or pertaining to the side
items.example: Collateralis adds col- to lateralis.
items.exampleCN: collateralis 在 lateralis 前加 col-。

items.example: col- is a sound-changed form of com-.
items.exampleCN: col- 是 com- 在 l 前的音变形式。

items.example: The word travels from side-by-side to pledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「并排」走到了「抵押品」。

items.example: Lateral movement is movement to the side.
items.exampleCN: lateral movement 就是向侧面运动。

items.example: A bilateral treaty sits between two states.
items.exampleCN: bilateral treaty 是两国之间的条约。

items.example: A unilateral decision is made by one side.
items.exampleCN: unilateral decision 是一方作出的决定。

items.example: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
items.exampleCN: 等边三角形有三条等长的边。

items.example: Lateralis uses -al as the adjective suffix.
items.exampleCN: Lateralis 用 -al 作形容词后缀。

items.example: The brain is lateralized for some functions.
items.exampleCN: 大脑某些功能是偏侧化的。

definition_en: the act of paying back money; an amount paid back
core_image: 一只手把钞票还给另一只手，钞票上贴着「paid back」的小红章
scene: 王女士每月工资到账后第一件事就是把一笔钱转到房贷账户里。The monthly repayment on her mortgage was higher than expected.
sceneCN: 这里 repayment 指「分期付款额」（第 4 个义项：每期需要偿还的金额）；句意为她房贷的月还款额比预想的高。图中可辨识物件：工资单、银行转账界面、房贷账户。

pos.zh: 还款（可数/不可数）

senses.title: the act of paying back
senses.definition: the act of returning money that was borrowed or owed
senses.definitionCN: 归还所借或所欠之钱的行为
senses.example: Repayment of the loan must be completed in three years.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款的偿还必须在三年内完成。
senses.why: repay + -ment yields the noun of the act.
senses.whyCN: repay 加 -ment 就是行为的名词。

senses.title: an amount paid back
senses.definition: a single sum of money returned to a creditor
senses.definitionCN: 还给债权人的一笔钱
senses.example: Each repayment reduced the outstanding balance.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次还款都减少了未结清的余额。
senses.why: The act names its typical result, the sum itself.
senses.whyCN: 行为指称其典型结果，即那笔金额本身。

senses.title: act of rewarding
senses.definition: the act of giving something in return for a favour or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 为答谢恩惠或善意而回报某物的行为
senses.example: Her repayment for the favour was a home-cooked meal.
senses.exampleCN: 她以一顿家常菜来报答这份恩惠。
senses.why: The 'pay back' sense is broadened from money to kindness.
senses.whyCN: 「还钱」义被拓宽到从金钱到善意。

senses.title: regular instalment
senses.definition: a regularly scheduled amount paid towards a debt
senses.definitionCN: 按计划定期支付的债务金额
senses.example: The loan had monthly repayments of two hundred dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款每月还款两百美元。
senses.why: Regular repayments are the usual structure of long-term debt.
senses.whyCN: 定期还款是长期债务的常见结构。

senses.title: full settlement
senses.definition: the final amount that closes out a debt
senses.definitionCN: 结清全部债务的最终金额
senses.example: A penalty applied to early repayment of the bond.
senses.exampleCN: 提前偿还债券需要支付罚金。
senses.why: The final act of repayment gets its own focus.
senses.whyCN: 偿还的最终行为被单独凸显出来。

senses.title: interest portion
senses.definition: the portion of a repayment that covers interest rather than principal
senses.definitionCN: 还款中覆盖利息而非本金的那部分
senses.example: In the early years most of the repayment went to interest.
senses.exampleCN: 在头几年，还款的大部分都用来付利息。
senses.why: A repayment can be split into parts; the interest slice is named separately.
senses.whyCN: 一笔还款可以分成几块；利息那块被单独指称。

senses.title: recoupment figuratively
senses.definition: recovery of an earlier loss or expenditure
senses.definitionCN: 回收此前的损失或支出
senses.example: The repayment of investors' confidence took years.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者信心的恢复花了数年。
senses.why: Abstract or non-monetary recovery borrows the repayment idea.
senses.whyCN: 抽象或非金钱层面的恢复借用了 repayment 的想法。

senses.title: schedule or plan
senses.definition: an agreed schedule of when amounts will be returned
senses.definitionCN: 约定的金额归还时间安排
senses.example: The repayment schedule stretched over thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 还款计划长达三十年。
senses.why: The plan of repayments takes the name of the repayments themselves.
senses.whyCN: 还款的计划也用了 repayment 的名字。

intro.en: Repayment is repay + -ment. Repay itself is re- 'back' + pay, which comes from Old French payer 'to pay, to pacify'.
intro.cn: repayment 是 repay 加 -ment。repay 本身是 re-「回」+ pay，而 pay 来自古法语 payer「支付、安抚」。

items.en: Latin re- 'back, again' was productive in Old French compound verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁语 re-「回、再」在古法语复合动词里很活跃。

items.en: Old French payer 'to pay, pacify' came from Latin pacare 'to make peace, appease', itself from pax 'peace'.
items.cn: 古法语 payer「支付、安抚」来自拉丁语 pacare「使和平、安抚」，后者来自 pax「和平」。

items.en: English pay entered around 1300 from Old French payer.
items.cn: 英语 pay 约 1300 年从古法语 payer 进入。

items.en: repay was formed in Middle English as re- 'back' + pay, first meaning 'pay back'.
items.cn: repay 在中古英语由 re-「回」+ pay 构成，最初意为「还回去」。

items.en: The suffix -ment (from Latin -mentum via French) turns verbs into nouns of action or result.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment（来自拉丁语 -mentum 经法语）把动词变成行为或结果的名词。

items.en: Solid etymology: re-, pay, and -ment are all well documented. The deeper link of pay to peace is often surprising but established.
items.cn: 词源可靠：re-、pay 与 -ment 均有充分文献。pay 与和平的深层联系常令人惊讶但已确立。

note.en: Look-alikes share the pay root; near meanings sit around money returned.
note.cn: 形近共享 pay 词根；近义围绕「返还的钱」展开。

entries.definition: To pay back; repayment is the noun form.
entries.definitionCN: 偿还；repayment 是它的名词。

entries.definition: To give money for something; repay adds the 'back' direction.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱买东西；repay 加了「回」的方向。

entries.definition: Money given, not necessarily back; repayment specifically returns what was owed.
entries.definitionCN: 给出的钱，不一定是还回去；repayment 特指归还所欠。

entries.definition: Informal; return of money or revenge.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式；还钱或报复。

entries.definition: Money returned for a purchase; repayment is to a lender or creditor.
entries.definitionCN: 购物退款；repayment 是还给贷款人或债主。

entries.definition: The final payment that closes a debt; repayment is any single part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 结清债务的最终付款；repayment 是其中任意一笔。

entries.definition: One regularly scheduled part of a repayment plan.
entries.definitionCN: 还款计划中按计划定期的一次。

entries.definition: Any reward or compensation for harm; repayment is specifically money returned.
entries.definitionCN: 对伤害的赔偿或回报；repayment 特指归还金钱。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: re- 'back' + pay 'to pay' + -ment 'action' = the action of paying back.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ pay「付」+ -ment「行为」= 还回去的行为。

normal.en: pay ultimately comes from Latin pax 'peace'; paying was originally appeasing.
normal.cn: pay 最终来自拉丁语 pax「和平」；pay 原本是安抚的意思。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: monthly repayment, early repayment, repayment schedule.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：monthly repayment 月供、early repayment 提前还款、repayment schedule 还款计划。

normal.en: repay, repayable, repayment are a tidy family.
normal.cn: repay、repayable、repayment 是整齐的同族。

normal.en: In an amortising loan, each repayment splits principal and interest.
normal.cn: 在分期偿还贷款里，每笔 repayment 都分成本金和利息。

abstract.en: Picture two hands: one takes, one gives back.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手：一只拿走，一只还回。

abstract.en: Picture a clock where each tick marks another repayment deadline.
abstract.cn: 想象一个时钟，每一格就是一次还款期限。

abstract.en: Picture Latin saying pax to your creditor after you pay.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁语说 pay 给债主后 peace 就来了。

examples.en: The monthly repayment rose sharply when the interest rate was reset.
examples.cn: 利率重新设定后，月供暴涨。

examples.en: Full repayment of the debt came four years ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 全额偿还比计划提前了四年。

examples.en: She received no repayment for the kindness she had shown the stranger.
examples.cn: 她对陌生人的善意没有得到任何回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（回）+ pay（付）+ -ment = 付回去的行为 → 还款

root: 拉丁语 re-「回」+ 古法语 payer「支付」（拉丁语 pacare「安抚」← pax「和平」）+ 法语 -ment 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the act of paying back → the amount → rewarding kindness → regular instalment → full settlement → interest portion → figurative recoupment → the schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从偿还行为 → 偿还金额 → 报答 → 定期分期还款 → 全额结清 → 利息部分 → 比喻的回收 → 还款计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand returns a stack of banknotes to another, a tiny clock ticks beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一叠钞票还给另一只手，旁边一个小钟在走。

branches.en: THE ACT: paying back what was owed.
branches.cn: 行为：偿还所欠。

branches.en: THE SUMS: any single amount or a regular one.
branches.cn: 金额：任意单笔或定期的一笔。

branches.en: THE FINAL ACT: full settlement, often with penalty if early.
branches.cn: 最终行为：全额结清，提前可能有罚金。

branches.en: NON-FINANCIAL USES: rewarding kindness or recovering confidence.
branches.cn: 非财务用法：报答善意或恢复信心。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: the interest portion and the plan itself.
branches.cn: 结构：利息那部分和还款计划本身。

intro.en: Repayment is repay + -ment; repay is re- + pay; pay comes from Latin pacare.
intro.cn: repayment 是 repay + -ment；repay 是 re- + pay；pay 来自拉丁语 pacare。

latinIntro.en: Pay ← Old French payer ← Latin pacare (to appease) ← pax (peace). re- is Latin; -ment is Latin -mentum.
latinIntro.cn: pay ← 古法语 payer ← 拉丁语 pacare（安抚）← pax（和平）。re- 来自拉丁语；-ment 来自拉丁语 -mentum。

items.exampleCN: pay 原本就是安抚债主。

items.example: pacare from pax 'peace'; paying calmed the debt.
items.exampleCN: pacare 来自 pax「和平」；付钱就能平息债务。

items.example: Repay is the verb of repayment.
items.exampleCN: repay 是 repayment 的动词。

items.example: -ment turns the verb into its noun.

items.example: The loan is repayable over five years.
items.exampleCN: 这笔贷款五年内可偿还。

items.meaning: the act of paying (not necessarily back)
items.example: Payment is broader than repayment.
items.exampleCN: payment 比 repayment 更宽。

items.example: The payee signs when receiving repayment.
items.exampleCN: 收款人收到 repayment 时要签字。

items.example: The payer of the repayment is the borrower.
items.exampleCN: repayment 的付款人是借款人。

items.example: The remote root of pay is peace.
items.exampleCN: pay 的遥远词根是和平。

definition_en: to pay back money owed; to give something in return for kindness or injury
core_image: 一只张开的手掌接到钱，另一张手掌上的欠款数字随之变小
scene: 小方大学时向亲戚借了一笔钱，毕业工作的第一个月就想把它还掉。He plans to repay the entire debt within two years.
sceneCN: 这里 repay 指「偿还借款」（第 1 个义项：归还所欠的钱）；句意为他计划在两年内还清全部债务。图中可辨识物件：借条、转账记录、日历。

pos.zh: 偿还；报答（及物/不及物均可）

senses.title: to pay back money
senses.definition: to give back money that was borrowed or owed
senses.definitionCN: 把借来的或欠下的钱还给对方
senses.example: She repaid the loan three months early.
senses.exampleCN: 她提前三个月还清了贷款。
senses.why: This is the basic re- + pay sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是 re- + pay 的基本义。

senses.title: to settle a debt
senses.definition: to discharge or settle an amount owed, whether money or another obligation
senses.definitionCN: 结清所欠金额，无论金钱或其他义务
senses.example: He repaid his debt to society by serving three years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过服刑三年来偿还对社会的债务。
senses.why: The monetary sense extends to any obligation one owes.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义延伸到任何亏欠的义务。

senses.title: to give back for kindness
senses.definition: to do or give something nice in return for a favour or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 为答谢恩惠或善意而做或给予美好的事物
senses.example: She repaid his kindness with a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一份礼物来报答他的善意。
senses.why: 'Pay back' moves from money to gratitude.
senses.whyCN: pay back 从金钱走到了感激。

senses.title: to return with interest
senses.definition: to return more than was borrowed or received
senses.definitionCN: 返还的比借入或收到的多
senses.example: I'll repay your generosity with interest.
senses.exampleCN: 我会加倍报答你的慷慨。
senses.why: The idea of repaying interest extends to any generous return.
senses.whyCN: 偿还利息的想法延伸到任何慷慨的回报。

senses.title: to compensate for injury
senses.definition: to make up for a harm or injury done to someone
senses.definitionCN: 弥补对某人造成的伤害
senses.example: The family repaid the stranger's carelessness with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人对陌生人的粗心给予了愤怒的「回报」。
senses.why: Paying back an injury is the dark side of the repay idea.
senses.whyCN: 偿还伤害是 repay 想法的阴暗面。

senses.title: to equal a benefit
senses.definition: to be worth enough to make up for a cost or sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 价值足以弥补代价或牺牲
senses.example: The joys of teaching repay the long hours.
senses.exampleCN: 教书的乐趣足以回报那些漫长的工作时间。
senses.why: Abstract value makes up for cost, like a repayment.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的价值弥补代价，就像 repayment 一样。

senses.title: to refund
senses.definition: to give money back because of a return or cancellation
senses.definitionCN: 因退货或取消而把钱还给对方
senses.example: The shop repaid the full amount when the product broke.
senses.exampleCN: 产品损坏后商店全额退款。
senses.why: A refund is a kind of repayment for money received.
senses.whyCN: 退款是偿还已收金额的一种形式。

senses.title: to respond in kind
senses.definition: to respond to an action with a similar action
senses.definitionCN: 以类似的行动回应某个行动
senses.example: If he insults you, don't repay him in the same coin.
senses.exampleCN: 如果他骂你，不要以牙还牙。
senses.why: Paying back an action mirrors the structure of repaying money.
senses.whyCN: 偿还一个行为在结构上跟还钱一样。

intro.en: Repay is a transparent compound: re- 'back' + pay. Pay itself comes from Old French payer 'to appease', which comes from Latin pacare.
intro.cn: repay 是清晰的复合：re-「回」+ pay。pay 来自古法语 payer「安抚」，后者来自拉丁语 pacare。

items.en: Latin re- 'back, again' formed many Middle English compound verbs.
items.cn: 拉丁语 re-「回、再」在中古英语构成很多复合动词。

items.en: Old French payer came from Latin pacare 'to appease, make peace', built on pax 'peace'.
items.cn: 古法语 payer 来自拉丁语 pacare「使和平、安抚」，由 pax「和平」构成。

items.en: English pay entered around 1300 from Old French.
items.cn: 英语 pay 约 1300 年从古法语进入。

items.en: repay was formed by early Middle English (around 1300) as a transparent compound of re- + pay.
items.cn: repay 在早期中古英语（约 1300）由 re- + pay 构成，是清晰的复合。

items.en: The past tense and past participle repaid follows an irregular pattern: repay → repaid by analogy with pay → paid.
items.cn: 过去式和过去分词 repaid 按不规则形式：repay → repaid，类比 pay → paid。

items.en: All etymology solid; the 'appease' origin of pay is well established in historical lexicography.
items.cn: 全部词源可靠；pay「安抚」的起源在历史词典学中已充分确立。

note.en: Look-alikes share the pay root; near meanings are ways of giving something back.
note.cn: 形近共享 pay 词根；近义是把某物还给对方的各种方式。

entries.definition: To give money; repay adds 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱；repay 加了「回」。

entries.definition: To play again; same re- prefix, different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 再玩一次；同 re- 前缀，不同第二成分。

entries.definition: To show; no re- prefix, different compound.
entries.definitionCN: 展示；没有 re- 前缀，另一个复合。

entries.definition: The past tense of repay, irregular like paid.
entries.definitionCN: repay 的过去式，不规则，跟 paid 一样。

entries.definition: To give something back in general; repay is mostly money or kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西还给对方，泛指；repay 多指钱或善意。

entries.definition: To give money back because of a return; repay covers any debt or kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 因退货而退钱；repay 覆盖任何债务或善意。

entries.definition: To compensate for harm or effort, not just money.
entries.definitionCN: 补偿伤害或努力，不限于金钱。

entries.definition: To respond to a favour with a favour; repay extends to money and harm too.
entries.definitionCN: 以恩惠回报恩惠；repay 也延伸到金钱和伤害。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: repay a loan, repay a favour, repay in full.

abstract.en: Picture a hand giving back coins while another hand's debt shrinks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手还回硬币，另一只手上的欠款就变小。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin creditor saying 'pax!' after being paid.
abstract.cn: 想象一个罗马债主收到钱后喊一声「和平了！」。

abstract.en: Picture an X on the debt note that fades as repayments come in.
abstract.cn: 想象借条上的欠款随着每一次还款在变淡。

examples.en: He will repay the loan with monthly instalments over three years.
examples.cn: 他将在三年内按月分期偿还这笔贷款。

examples.en: She repaid her old teacher's encouragement by becoming an educator herself.
examples.cn: 她成为一名教育工作者，以此回报老恩师的鼓励。

examples.en: Will the joy of living abroad repay the disruption to her career?
examples.cn: 在国外生活的快乐能弥补事业上的中断吗？

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold: pay back money → settle any obligation → repay kindness → generous return → repay harm → abstract cost-benefit → refund → respond in kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开：还钱 → 结清任何义务 → 报答善意 → 慷慨回报 → 偿还伤害 → 抽象上的成本收益 → 退款 → 以同样方式回应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand pushes coins into another, a debt note behind them loses value.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把硬币推给另一只手，身后的借条在贬值。

branches.en: THE MONETARY CORE: returning borrowed money.
branches.cn: 金钱核心：归还借来的钱。

branches.en: ANY OBLIGATION: debts to society, not only banks.
branches.cn: 任何义务：对社会的债，不只是银行。

branches.en: POSITIVE RETURNS: kindness rewarded, generosity returned with interest.
branches.cn: 正面回报：善意得到报答，慷慨得到加倍回报。

branches.en: NEGATIVE RETURNS: harm repaid, eye for an eye.
branches.cn: 负面回报：伤害被偿还，以牙还牙。

branches.en: ABSTRACT AND COMMERCIAL: abstract value repays a cost, refunds are a commercial repay.
branches.cn: 抽象与商业：抽象价值回报代价，退款是商业中的 repay。
