definition_zh: 分期付款；一期；一集；部分
definition_en: one of several regular payments for a debt; one part of a series
core_image: 一本日历，每个月都被划掉一个方格，方格上标着小小的金额数字
scene: 小丽想买一台最新款的电脑，商店说可以分十期付，每期两百块。She decided the installment plan was easier than paying all at once.
sceneCN: 这里 installment 指「分期付款的一期」（第 1 个义项：债务的定期分期付款之一）；句意为他们选择分月付而不是一次性付清。图中可辨识物件：日历、电脑、分期付款收据。

pos.zh: 分期付款（可数）；一集（可数）

senses.title: regular debt payment
senses.definition: one of a series of scheduled payments to settle a debt
senses.definitionCN: 结清债务的一系列预定付款之一
senses.example: The loan required twelve monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款要求分十二个月偿还。
senses.why: The root is install, 'to set up', as in setting up a schedule of payments.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 install「设立」，就像设立一个付款日程。

senses.title: part of a purchase
senses.definition: one part of the price of an item paid over time
senses.definitionCN: 一件商品的价格中按时间分批支付的一部分
senses.example: They bought the fridge on easy instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以轻松分期的方式买下了冰箱。
senses.why: A purchase that you set up with a payment plan.
senses.whyCN: 通过付款计划设立的一笔消费。

senses.title: episode of a story
senses.definition: one episode of a serial story, television show or podcast
senses.definitionCN: 连载故事、电视剧或播客的一集
senses.example: The novel was published in monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说按月连载。
senses.why: A story set up to come out piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一段一段推出的故事。

senses.title: stage of a plan
senses.definition: one stage of an overall plan or project
senses.definitionCN: 整体计划或项目的一个阶段
senses.example: The first instalment of the highway opened in 2024.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路的一期在 2024 年通车。
senses.why: A large work set up as a series of smaller bits.
senses.whyCN: 一项大工程被设立成若干小块。

senses.title: artwork installation
senses.definition: a large artwork set up in a specific space
senses.definitionCN: 设立在特定空间里的大型艺术作品
senses.example: The museum commissioned a new instalment.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆委托创作了一件新的装置作品。
senses.why: A work that is installed, set up in a space.
senses.whyCN: 一件被 install、设立在空间里的作品。

senses.title: initial payment
senses.definition: the first payment in a series
senses.definitionCN: 一系列付款中的第一笔
senses.example: The first instalment was due on delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 首期款在交货时到期。
senses.why: The first of the scheduled pieces.
senses.whyCN: 预定的几块中的第一块。

senses.title: supplement or tranche
senses.definition: a supplementary sum of money released over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间分批释放的一笔追加资金
senses.example: The donor promised a second instalment in 2026.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者承诺 2026 年捐出第二期款项。
senses.why: Money set up to come in slices.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一片片进来的钱。

senses.title: scheduled meeting
senses.definition: a scheduled session of a course or training programme
senses.definitionCN: 课程或培训项目预定的一节课
senses.example: The leadership course had six fortnightly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领导力课程分六次，每两周一次。
senses.why: A course set up as pieces over time.
senses.whyCN: 一门被设立成若干块、按时间推出的课程。

intro.en: Instalment comes from install 'to set up, arrange' + -ment. Install itself came from Old French installer, from Latin installare.
intro.cn: instalment 来自 install「设立、安排」+ -ment。install 本身来自古法语 installer，后者来自拉丁语 installare。

items.en: Latin installare meant 'to place in a seat, to install in an office'; it was in- 'in' + stallum 'seat, stall'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 installare 意为「安置在座位上、任命」，由 in-「在……里」+ stallum「座位、栏」构成。

items.en: Old French installer meant 'to install, establish'.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 意为「安装、设立」。

items.en: English install was borrowed around 1400 meaning 'to place formally, to establish'.
items.cn: 英语 install 约 1400 年从古法语借入，意为「正式安置、设立」。

items.en: Instalment was formed from install + -ment around 1560, first meaning 'an arrangement, a setting up'.
items.cn: instalment 约 1560 年由 install + -ment 构成，最初意为「一个安排、一次设立」。

items.en: The 'partial payment' sense developed from the idea of 'setting up a debt to be paid in parts', by the 18th century.
items.cn: 「分期付款」义来自「设立一笔要分几块还的债」的想法，18 世纪形成。

items.en: Installment (US) and instalment (UK) are both standard; the Latin root stallum is well attested.
items.cn: 美式 installment 和英式 instalment 都是标准拼写；拉丁词根 stallum 来源可靠。

note.en: Look-alikes share the install root; near meanings are one of several payments or parts.
note.cn: 形近共享 install 词根；近义是若干付款或部分中的一个。

entries.definition: To set up or place; instalment is the noun of a piece of what is set up.
entries.definitionCN: 设立、安置；instalment 是被设立的东西的一块。

entries.definition: The act of installing, or a facility set up.
entries.definitionCN: 安装行为，或设立的设施。

entries.definition: A person who installs something.
entries.definitionCN: 安装工。

entries.definition: A seat or enclosure, from the Latin stallum.
entries.definitionCN: 座位或栏，来自拉丁语 stallum。

entries.definition: Any amount paid, not necessarily part of a scheduled series.
entries.definitionCN: 任何支付的金额，不一定是预定系列中的一部分。

entries.definition: One scheduled piece of a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 更大整体中预定好的一块。

entries.definition: A slice of money released over time; usually financial.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间分批释放的一笔资金块；通常指财务。

entries.definition: One part of a serial story, same as the story sense of instalment.
entries.definitionCN: 连载故事的一部分，跟 instalment 的故事义相同。

normal.en: install 'to set up' + -ment = a piece of what has been set up (schedule, series, debt).
normal.cn: install「设立」+ -ment = 被设立的东西（日程、系列、债务）中的一块。

normal.en: stallum is Latin for 'seat, stall'; installare means 'to place in a seat'.
normal.cn: stallum 拉丁语意为「座位、栏」；installare 意为「安置在座位上」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: monthly instalment, pay in instalments, instalment plan.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：monthly instalment 月供、pay in instalments 分期付、instalment plan 分期方案。

normal.en: install, installation, instalment are a tidy family.
normal.cn: install、installation、instalment 是整齐的同族。

normal.en: US uses -ll-: installment; UK uses -l-: instalment.
normal.cn: 美式双 l 拼 installment，英式单 l 拼 instalment。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with bricks being laid one by one, each brick an instalment.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙一块块砌起来，每一块砖就是一期。

abstract.en: Picture a judge installing a judge on the bench, then the bench splits into twelve pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法官坐在宝座上，然后宝座分裂成十二块。

abstract.en: Picture each month a piece of your debt falls off.
abstract.cn: 想象每个月你的债务就掉下一块。

examples.en: She chose an interest-free instalment plan to buy her first camera.
examples.cn: 她选择了免息分期方案买下了自己的第一台相机。

examples.en: The author released the novel in weekly instalments through an online platform.
examples.cn: 作者通过网络平台把这部小说按周连载。

examples.en: Only after the final instalment was paid did the title to the car transfer to her.
examples.cn: 只有在最后一期付清后，汽车的所有权才转移到她名下。

dict_mnemonic.text: install（设立）+ -ment = 被设立的一件事被拆成几块 → 分期

root: 拉丁语 installare（in-「在……里」+ stallum「座位、栏」）→ 古法语 installer → 英语 install + -ment → instalment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses progress from scheduled debt payment → part of a purchase → story episode → project stage → artwork → initial payment → supplementary funds → course session.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从预定债务付款 → 购买款的一部分 → 故事一集 → 项目阶段 → 装置艺术 → 首期 → 追加资金 → 课程一节课。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar where each month you place one small coin on the debt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本日历，每个月你都往债务上放一枚小硬币。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL SLICE: one part of a payment plan for debt or purchase.
branches.cn: 财务上的一块：债务或购买款付款计划中的一部分。

branches.en: THE STORY SLICE: one episode of a serial work.
branches.cn: 故事上的一块：连载作品的一集。

branches.en: THE CONSTRUCTION SLICE: a project stage or an artwork installation.
branches.cn: 工程上的一块：项目阶段或装置艺术。

branches.en: THE FUND SLICE: the first or a supplementary tranche.
branches.cn: 资金上的一块：首期或追加的一笔。

branches.en: THE EDUCATIONAL SLICE: one scheduled session of a course.
branches.cn: 教育上的一块：课程的一节预定课。

intro.en: Installment = install + -ment. Install ← French installer ← Latin installare.
intro.cn: installment = install + -ment。install ← 法 installer ← 拉丁 installare。

latinIntro.en: Latin installare = in- + stallum. stallum = seat, stall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 installare = in- + stallum。stallum = 座位、栏。

items.example: You install a schedule of payments.
items.exampleCN: 你设立一个付款日程。

items.meaning: a piece of what is installed
items.example: Each payment is one instalment of the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 每一次付款就是日程里的一期。

items.example: The root is a physical seat or stall.
items.exampleCN: 词根是一个物理的座位或栏。

items.example: in- puts you into the stallum.
items.exampleCN: in- 把你放进 stallum。

items.structure: Old English steall, related to Latin stallum
items.meaning: a seat, a booth, or to be stuck
items.example: Stall shares a root with Latin stallum.
items.exampleCN: stall 与拉丁语 stallum 同根。

items.meaning: the act of installing or a facility
items.example: A power station is an installation.
items.exampleCN: 发电站是一座 installation。

items.example: The installer came to fit the new dishwasher.
items.exampleCN: 安装工来装新洗碗机。

items.example: Instalment is the result of install + -ment.
items.exampleCN: Instalment 是 install + -ment 的结果。

items.example: Installation uses the different suffix -ation.
items.exampleCN: Installation 用的是另一个后缀 -ation。

items.example: Reinstall the software if it stalls.
items.exampleCN: 如果软件卡住了就重装。

latinEntries.meaning: to place in a seat; to install

definition_en: an arrangement to compensate for possible loss or damage; protection provided by such an arrangement
core_image: 一把打开的大伞，伞面上写着各种意外：火灾、车祸、疾病，伞下站着一家人
scene: 小张给新买的摩托车去买一份全保，保险经纪在白板上画满了各种承保的风险项。Insurance protects you against large, unexpected losses.
sceneCN: 这里 insurance 指「保险保障」（第 1 个义项：对可能损失的经济补偿安排）；句意为 insurance 保护你免受大额意外损失。图中可辨识物件：伞形图表、保单、白板上的风险项。

pos.zh: 保险（不可数；可数时指各类保险）

senses.title: arrangement for loss compensation
senses.definition: an arrangement in which one party promises to compensate another for specified losses
senses.definitionCN: 一方承诺为另一方补偿特定损失的安排
senses.example: Most homeowners carry fire insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 多数房主都投保了火险。
senses.why: in- + sure = make safe; insurance keeps you sure against loss.
senses.whyCN: in- + sure 就是使安全；insurance 让你免于损失的不确定。

senses.title: protection provided
senses.definition: the protection or cover given by an insurance arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 由保险安排所提供的保护或保障
senses.example: Her health insurance ran out when she quit her job.
senses.exampleCN: 她辞职后医保就过期了。
senses.why: The arrangement names its effect, the cover itself.
senses.whyCN: 安排指代其效果，即保障本身。

senses.title: the insurance industry
senses.definition: the business of providing insurance as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体上提供保险的行业
senses.example: The insurance industry employs over two million people.
senses.exampleCN: 保险业雇用了两百多万人。
senses.why: The whole business takes the name of its core product.
senses.whyCN: 整个行业用了其核心产品的名字。

senses.title: an insurance policy
senses.definition: a specific contract providing cover
senses.definitionCN: 一份具体的提供保障的合同
senses.example: He took out a new insurance policy on his home.
senses.exampleCN: 他为家里买了一份新保单。
senses.why: One specific contract is a single insurance.
senses.whyCN: 一份具体的合同就是一份 insurance。

senses.title: the amount insured
senses.definition: the amount of money that will be paid out if loss occurs
senses.definitionCN: 发生损失时将要赔付的金额
senses.example: The insurance on his life policy was one million dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 他的寿险保额是一百万美元。
senses.why: The policy names the amount it promises.
senses.whyCN: 保单也指代它承诺的金额。

senses.title: form of bet, figuratively
senses.definition: something done to reduce risk, like an insurance policy
senses.definitionCN: 为降低风险而做的事，就像一张保单
senses.example: Buying both candidates' books is my insurance against losing interest.
senses.exampleCN: 两个候选人的书都买，就是我防止失去兴趣的「保险」。
senses.why: Any risk-mitigating action borrows the insurance idea.
senses.whyCN: 任何降低风险的行为都借用了保险的想法。

senses.title: reinsurance
senses.definition: insurance that an insurer buys from another insurer to spread risk
senses.definitionCN: 保险公司从另一家购买以分散风险的保险
senses.example: Reinsurance let the small insurer survive the hurricane.
senses.exampleCN: 再保险让小保险公司撑过了飓风。
senses.why: Insurance for insurers, layered on top.
senses.whyCN: 给保险公司自己买的保险，叠加上去。

senses.title: self-insurance
senses.definition: setting aside money to cover your own losses rather than buying insurance
senses.definitionCN: 自己留钱来赔损失，而不是买保险
senses.example: Some large companies practise self-insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 有些大公司实行自保。
senses.why: A variant of insurance where you are your own insurer.
senses.whyCN: 保险的一种变体，你自己就是自己的保险公司。

intro.en: Insurance comes from insure, which is in- 'into' + sure 'certain'. To insure is to make someone sure (against loss).
intro.cn: insurance 来自 insure，即 in-「使变成」+ sure「确定」。insure 就是使某人确信（不会遭受损失）。

items.en: Latin in- could be causative, turning an adjective into a verb: in- + adjectival root = 'make ...'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 in- 可以是使役的，把形容词变成动词：in- + 形容词词根 =「使……」。

items.en: Sure came through Old French seur from Latin securus 'free from care', itself from se- 'without' + cura 'care'.
items.cn: sure 经古法语 seur 来自拉丁语 securus「免于关心的」，后者由 se-「无」+ cura「关心」构成。

items.en: Middle English ensured 'made certain' and insured 'made safe against loss' split off by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 ensured「使确定」和 insured「使免受损失」在 17 世纪分叉。

items.en: Insurance as the noun of the arrangement appeared in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 作为这种安排名词的 insurance 出现于 17 世纪。

items.en: Life insurance developed in the 18th century; health insurance in the 20th.
items.cn: 人寿保险发展于 18 世纪，医疗保险于 20 世纪。

items.en: All etymology solid; securus is well attested.
items.cn: 全部词源可靠；securus 有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the sure root; near meanings are ways to reduce risk.
note.cn: 形近共享 sure 词根；近义是降低风险的各种方式。

entries.definition: To provide insurance for; insurance is the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 给……上保险；insurance 是这种安排。

entries.definition: To make certain, not necessarily against loss.
entries.definitionCN: 确保某事，不一定针对损失。

entries.definition: Certain, free from doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的、无疑的。

entries.definition: To tell someone something confidently; not financial.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地告诉某人某事；与财务无关。

entries.definition: A specific insurance contract; insurance is the whole system or a type.
entries.definitionCN: 一份具体的保险合同；insurance 是整个体系或一个类型。

entries.definition: Any safeguard; insurance is a specific financial safeguard.
entries.definitionCN: 任何保障；insurance 是特定的财务保障。

entries.definition: A manufacturer's guarantee on a product, not from an insurer.
entries.definitionCN: 厂商对产品的保证，不是保险公司出的。

entries.definition: A financial position taken to offset risk, similar to insurance in function.
entries.definitionCN: 为抵消风险而持有的财务头寸，功能类似保险。

normal.en: in- + sure = make sure / safe against loss.
normal.cn: in- + sure = 使确信/使免受损失。

normal.en: sure ← French seur ← Latin securus (se- 'without' + cura 'care').
normal.cn: sure ← 法 seur ← 拉丁 securus（se-「无」+ cura「关心」）。

normal.en: insure (financial) vs ensure (general certainty) vs assure (reassure a person).
normal.cn: insure（财务）vs ensure（一般确定）vs assure（向人保证）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: health insurance, life insurance, insurance policy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：health insurance 医保、life insurance 寿险、insurance policy 保单。

normal.en: insurer, insured, insurant are the people side.
normal.cn: insurer、insured、insurant 是与人相关的同族。

abstract.en: Picture a big umbrella that opens when rain (loss) starts to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一把大雨伞，一有雨（损失）就撑开。

abstract.en: Picture Latin securus: no cura (care) left.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁 securus：一点关心都没有。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake between insurer and insured under the umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象保险公司和被保险人在伞下握手。

examples.en: Without health insurance, a single serious illness could bankrupt a family.
examples.cn: 没有医保，一场大病就能让一个家庭破产。

examples.en: The insurance policy did not cover the flood because the area was a known floodplain.
examples.cn: 这份保单不承保水灾，因为该地区是已知的洪泛平原。

examples.en: Insurance companies raised premiums after a string of costly natural disasters.
examples.cn: 在一连串代价高昂的自然灾害后，保险公司提高了保费。

dict_mnemonic.text: in-（使）+ sure（安全确定）= 使人安全确定的安排 → 保险

root: 拉丁语 securus（se-「无」+ cura「关心」）→ 古法语 seur → 英语 sure；加 in- 构成 insure「使安全」；insurance 为其名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the arrangement → the protection → the industry → a specific policy → the amount → figurative risk mitigation → reinsurance → self-insurance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从安排 → 保障 → 行业 → 一份具体保单 → 金额 → 比喻的风险降低 → 再保险 → 自保。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large umbrella opened over people, shielding them from falling coins labelled 'loss'.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把大伞撑在人们头顶，挡着落下来写着「损失」的硬币。

branches.en: THE CORE: the arrangement and the cover it provides.
branches.cn: 核心：安排与其提供的保障。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRY: the whole business of providing cover.
branches.cn: 行业：提供保障的整个产业。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT AND ITS VALUE: a specific policy and the sum it promises.
branches.cn: 合同与价值：一份具体保单及其承诺的金额。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE USE: any risk-reducing action.
branches.cn: 比喻用法：任何降低风险的行为。

branches.en: VARIANTS: reinsurance (insurer's insurance) and self-insurance (your own insurer).
branches.cn: 变体：再保险（保险公司的保险）与自保（你自己当保险公司）。

intro.en: Insurance = insure + -ance; insure = in- + sure; sure ← securus.
intro.cn: insurance = insure + -ance；insure = in- + sure；sure ← securus。

latinIntro.en: securus (se- 'without' + cura 'care'). in- is Latin causative prefix.
latinIntro.cn: securus（se-「无」+ cura「关心」）。in- 是拉丁语使役前缀。

items.example: in- turns sure into a verb.
items.exampleCN: in- 把 sure 变成动词。

items.example: sure = free from care or doubt.
items.exampleCN: sure = 免于关心或疑虑。

items.example: se- + cura = no care.
items.exampleCN: se- + cura = 没有关心。

items.example: Medical cura became cure.
items.exampleCN: 医疗 cura 变成了英语 cure。

items.example: You insure a house against fire.
items.exampleCN: 你给房子保火险。

items.example: -ance turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: -ance 把动词变成名词。

items.example: Ensure the door is locked; insure the house.
items.exampleCN: Ensure 门要锁；insure 房子要保。

items.example: Assure the child that everything is fine.
items.exampleCN: Assure 孩子一切都好。

items.example: Insurance uses -ance; assurance does too.
items.exampleCN: insurance 用 -ance；assurance 也用。

items.example: Reinsurance lets insurers share big risks.
items.exampleCN: 再保险让保险公司分担大风险。

definition_zh: 保险人；承保人；保险公司
definition_en: a person or company that provides insurance and promises to compensate for losses
core_image: 一把大伞举在人群头上，举伞的人胸前别着一块写着保险公司名字的牌子
scene: 车主的车在暴雨中被泡坏，他拨通了保单上的客服电话。The insurer promised to cover the repairs within ten days.
sceneCN: 这里 insurer 指「保险公司」（第 1 个义项：提供保险并承诺补偿损失的公司）；句意为 insurer 承诺十天内赔付维修费。图中可辨识物件：破损的车、保单、客服电话。

pos.zh: 保险人；承保人（可数）

collocations.zh: 最后承保人（再保险机制）

senses.title: insurance company
senses.definition: a business that sells insurance policies to the public
senses.definitionCN: 向公众出售保单的企业
senses.example: The insurer raised rates after the fire losses.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾损失后保险公司涨了费率。
senses.why: The suffix -er on insure names the one who does the insuring.
senses.whyCN: insure 加 -er 就叫那个做 insure 事的人。

senses.title: individual underwriter
senses.definition: a person, often a wealthy individual, who accepts insurance risk directly
senses.definitionCN: 通常是富人，直接接受保险风险的人
senses.example: Lloyd's of London still uses individual insurers called Names.
senses.exampleCN: 伦敦劳合社仍使用称为 Names 的个人承保人。
senses.why: Not all insurers are corporations; individuals still take risk.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有保险人都是公司；个人也承担风险。

senses.title: government insurer
senses.definition: a government agency that provides insurance for special areas
senses.definitionCN: 在特定领域提供保险的政府机构
senses.example: The FDIC is the federal insurer of bank deposits.
senses.exampleCN: FDIC 是联邦银行存款的保险人。
senses.why: Government also insures things that the private sector will not.
senses.whyCN: 政府也为私营部门不愿承保的事提供保险。

senses.title: reinsurer
senses.definition: an insurer that provides insurance to other insurers
senses.definitionCN: 给其他保险公司提供保险的保险公司
senses.example: Major catastrophes can strain the whole network of insurers.
senses.exampleCN: 重大灾害会让整个保险人网络绷紧。
senses.why: Insurers themselves need insurance from someone further up.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司自己也需要上面有人给他保险。

senses.title: who promises to indemnify
senses.definition: any party that promises to pay compensation for a specified loss
senses.definitionCN: 承诺为特定损失支付赔偿的任何一方
senses.example: The contract named the offshore company as sole insurer.
senses.exampleCN: 合同指定那家离岸公司为唯一保险人。
senses.why: The functional sense: whoever performs the insurance role.
senses.whyCN: 功能义：任何执行保险角色的一方。

senses.title: insurer of last resort
senses.definition: a fund that pays when no other insurer can, after a systemic crisis
senses.definitionCN: 在系统性危机后、其他保险人都不能赔时支付的基金
senses.example: The state fund acts as insurer of last resort for quake losses.
senses.exampleCN: 国家基金充当地震损失的最后承保人。
senses.why: A backstop when every insurer fails.
senses.whyCN: 当所有保险人都倒下时的最后保障。

senses.title: medical insurer
senses.definition: a health plan or HMO that provides medical coverage
senses.definitionCN: 提供医疗保障的健康计划或组织
senses.example: His medical insurer covered ninety percent of the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 他的医保机构支付了百分之九十的治疗费。
senses.why: Health insurers are a specialised sub-type.
senses.whyCN: 医疗保险是一个专业子类型。

senses.title: life insurer
senses.definition: a company that pays on the death of the insured
senses.definitionCN: 被保险人死亡时支付的公司
senses.example: Life insurers use mortality tables to set premiums.
senses.exampleCN: 人寿保险公司用生命表来设定保费。
senses.why: Another specialised line of insurance.
senses.whyCN: 另一条专业化的保险线。

intro.en: Insurer = insure + -er. Insure is in- (causative) + sure. The noun 'one who insures' was formed in the 17th century.
intro.cn: insurer = insure + -er。insure 是 in-（使役）+ sure。表示「做保险者」的名词形成于 17 世纪。

items.en: Middle English in- (causative) + sure made the verb insure, meaning 'make safe'.
items.cn: 中古英语 in-（使役）+ sure 构成动词 insure，意为「使安全」。

items.en: Adding the agent suffix -er gave insurer: 'one who makes (someone) safe against loss'.
items.cn: 加施事后缀 -er 得 insurer：「使某人免受损失的人」。

items.en: The earliest English use of insurer appears around 1650 in ship insurance contracts.
items.cn: insurer 在英语中最早见于约 1650 年的船只保险合同。

items.en: By the 19th century most insurers were corporations, not private individuals.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，多数保险人已是公司而非个人。

items.en: The reinsurance layer developed in the 19th century as insurers needed to spread risk.
items.cn: 再保险层发展于 19 世纪，因为保险公司需要分散风险。

items.en: All etymology solid, derivative, straightforward.
items.cn: 词源可靠，是直接的派生词。

note.en: Look-alikes are other sure-family words; near meanings are parties to an insurance contract.
note.cn: 形近是 sure 家族的其他词；近义是保险合同的另一方。

entries.definition: To provide insurance; insurer does it for others.
entries.definitionCN: 提供保险；insurer 是替人做这件事的一方。

entries.definition: The protected party, opposite of insurer.
entries.definitionCN: 被保障的一方，与 insurer 对立。

entries.definition: General 'make certain', not financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般的「使确定」，不涉及财务。

entries.definition: To tell confidently; no risk or money involved.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地告诉人；不涉及风险或金钱。

entries.definition: The one who buys the insurance from the insurer.
entries.definitionCN: 从 insurer 手里买保险的人。

entries.definition: An insurer who evaluates and accepts risk, often within a company.
entries.definitionCN: 在公司内评估并接受风险的专业保险人。

entries.definition: One who arranges insurance between insured and insurer; takes no risk.
entries.definitionCN: 在 insured 和 insurer 之间撮合的中介；不承担风险。

entries.definition: An insurer that provides insurance to other insurers.
entries.definitionCN: 给其他保险公司提供保险的 insurer。

normal.en: insure + -er = the one who insures.
normal.cn: insure + -er = 做保险的那一个。

normal.en: insurer promises; insured is promised.
normal.cn: insurer 承诺；insured 是被承诺的那方。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: insurer of last resort, leading insurer, reinsurer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：insurer of last resort 最后承保人、leading insurer 头部保险公司、reinsurer 再保险公司。

normal.en: -er is the agent suffix; insurer does the action of insure.
normal.cn: -er 是施事后缀；insurer 做 insure 的动作。

normal.en: Major insurers: Lloyd's, AIG, Allianz.
normal.cn: 主要 insurer：劳合社、友邦、安联。

abstract.en: Picture a giant holding an umbrella over hundreds of tiny people.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨人举着大伞，下面有几百个小人。

abstract.en: Picture the insurer and the insured shaking hands under the policy tree.
abstract.cn: 想象 insurer 和 insured 在保单树下握手。

abstract.en: Picture coins flowing into the insurer's coffers and flowing out to pay claims.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币流进 insurer 的金库，再流出去赔理赔。

examples.en: Her insurer denied the claim because the policy excluded water damage from outside the floodplain.
examples.cn: 她的保险公司拒赔，因为保单排除了洪泛区外的水灾损失。

examples.en: Smaller insurers banded together to form a risk pool for hurricanes.
examples.cn: 较小的保险公司组成了一个飓风风险共保组织。

examples.en: The federal insurer stepped in to protect depositors when the bank failed.
examples.cn: 银行倒闭后，联邦保险人介入保护储户。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从公司 insurer → 个人承保人 → 政府保险人 → 再保险公司 → 任何承诺赔偿的一方 → 最后承保人 → 医保机构 → 寿险公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a friendly giant holding an umbrella over a crowd of insured people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个友好的巨人举着伞，下面是一群被保险人。

branches.en: THE CORPORATE CORE: the public insurance company.
branches.cn: 公司核心：面向公众的保险公司。

branches.en: THE TRADITIONAL FORM: individual underwriters, especially at Lloyd's.
branches.cn: 传统形式：个人承保人，尤其在劳合社。

branches.en: THE NON-PROFIT AND FUNCTIONAL: government insurers or any party that promises indemnity.
branches.cn: 非营利与功能义：政府保险人或任何承诺赔偿的一方。

branches.en: THE BACKSTOP: reinsurance and the insurer of last resort.
branches.cn: 最后保障：再保险与最后承保人。

branches.cn: 专业领域：医保与寿险公司。

intro.cn: insurer = insure + -er。insure = in- + sure。

items.example: -er marks the actor.
items.exampleCN: -er 标出了行为者。

items.example: The insured receives the cover.
items.exampleCN: insured 接受保障。

items.example: Teacher, writer, insurer all use -er.
items.exampleCN: teacher、writer、insurer 都用 -er。

items.exampleCN: insured 就是被 insure 过的。

items.meaningCN: 在下面签字接受风险的人

items.example: The policyholder pays premiums.
items.exampleCN: policyholder 付保费。

items.example: Reinsurers sit above primary insurers.
items.exampleCN: 再保险公司在主承保人上面。

items.example: Brokers arrange between parties.
items.exampleCN: 经纪人在各方之间撮合。

items.example: Sure's Latin root means carefree.
items.exampleCN: sure 的拉丁词根就是无忧无虑。

definition_zh: 被保险人；投保的；受保障的
definition_en: a person or thing covered by insurance; covered by insurance
core_image: 一个人身上披着一件印有保险公司标志的长斗篷，斗篷上写着 covered
scene: 奶奶住院的医疗费大部分被报销了，她感叹幸好五年前买了那一份保险。The insured received the full payment promised in the policy.
sceneCN: 这里 insured 指「被保险人」（第 1 个义项：被保险保障覆盖的人）；句意为 insured 收到了保单承诺的全额赔付。图中可辨识物件：医院收据、保险单、报销支票。

pos.zh: 投保的；受保障的
被保险人（可数）

senses.title: person covered by insurance
senses.definition: a person who has bought insurance and is protected against specified losses
senses.definitionCN: 购买了保险并在特定损失下受到保护的人
senses.example: The insured must pay premiums every month.
senses.exampleCN: 被保险人每月都要交保费。
senses.why: insure + -ed = one who has been insured.
senses.whyCN: insure 加 -ed 就是被 insure 过的人。

senses.title: property covered
senses.definition: a house, car or other asset covered by insurance
senses.definitionCN: 被保险覆盖的房屋、汽车或其他资产
senses.example: The insured was destroyed in the hurricane.
senses.exampleCN: 被保险的财产在飓风中被毁。
senses.why: In practice, insured can name the thing as well as the person.
senses.whyCN: 在实际使用中，insured 可以指物也可以指人。

senses.title: group insured under one policy
senses.definition: multiple people covered under a single group policy
senses.definitionCN: 在一张团体保单下被保障的多人
senses.example: All employees became insured under the company plan.
senses.exampleCN: 所有员工都被公司计划纳入保障。
senses.why: A group policy covers many insureds at once.
senses.whyCN: 一张团体保单同时覆盖许多 insured。

senses.title: fully insured
senses.definition: having insurance that covers the full value or risk
senses.definitionCN: 拥有覆盖全部价值或风险的保险的
senses.example: He was fully insured before taking the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发旅行前他全额投保了。
senses.why: The adjective sense describes the state of being covered.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义描述被保障的状态。

senses.title: self-insured
senses.definition: setting aside your own money to cover losses, not buying insurance
senses.definitionCN: 自己留钱赔损失，而不是买保险
senses.example: Large firms often remain self-insured for small risks.
senses.exampleCN: 大公司常对小风险实行自保。
senses.why: You are your own insurer, so you are self-insured.
senses.whyCN: 你自己就是自己的 insurer，所以你是 self-insured。

senses.title: named insured
senses.definition: a specific person or entity explicitly named in the policy
senses.definitionCN: 保单中明确指名的个人或实体
senses.example: The named insured was the company, not its directors.
senses.exampleCN: 指名被保险人是公司，不是其董事。
senses.why: Policies distinguish the named from additional insureds.
senses.whyCN: 保单区分指名被保险人和附加被保险人。

senses.title: additional insured
senses.definition: someone added to the policy after the named insured
senses.definitionCN: 在指名被保险人之后被加入保单的人
senses.example: The contractor added the client as an additional insured.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商把客户加为附加被保险人。
senses.why: Additional layers of protection, still insured.
senses.whyCN: 额外的保障层，仍然是 insured。

senses.title: uninsured counterpoint
senses.definition: the opposite of uninsured; a person or thing without cover
senses.definitionCN: uninsured 的反面；没有保障的人或物
senses.example: More than ten percent of drivers remain uninsured.
senses.exampleCN: 超过一成的司机没有投保。
senses.why: By contrast: insured and uninsured form a pair.
senses.whyCN: 对比之下：insured 和 uninsured 构成一对。

intro.en: Insured is the past participle of insure, used as an adjective and noun: 'having been made safe (against loss)'.
intro.cn: insured 是 insure 的过去分词，用作形容词和名词：「已经被使安全（免受损失）的」。

items.en: insure (verb) + -ed (past participle suffix) = insured.
items.cn: insure（动词）+ -ed（过去分词后缀）= insured。

items.en: By the 17th century insured was used as an adjective meaning 'covered by insurance'.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪 insured 已用作形容词，意为「被保险覆盖的」。

items.en: Using the participle as a noun is common in English: the insured = the person insured.
items.cn: 英语里把分词用作名词很常见：the insured = 被保险的那个人。

items.en: Compounds like uninsured, self-insured, underinsured developed later.
items.cn: uninsured、self-insured、underinsured 等复合词后来才出现。

items.en: Insurant, another noun form, is borrowed from French and is less common.
items.cn: insurant 是另一个名词形式，借自法语，较少用。

items.en: All etymology straightforward; no disputed roots.
items.cn: 词源直接明了，无争议词根。

note.en: Look-alikes are other -ed participles of sure-family verbs; near meanings are related parties in insurance.
note.cn: 形近是 sure 家族动词的其他 -ed 分词；近义是保险中的相关方。

entries.definition: Past participle of ensure 'make certain'; not financial.
entries.definitionCN: ensure「使确定」的过去分词；与财务无关。

entries.definition: Past participle of assure; also means confident.
entries.definitionCN: assure 的过去分词；也指自信的。

entries.definition: Certain, not a participle.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的，不是分词。

entries.definition: Not covered by insurance.
entries.definitionCN: 没有被保险覆盖的。

entries.definition: Same meaning as insured, borrowed from French insurant.
entries.definitionCN: 与 insured 同义的法语借词。

entries.definition: One who receives the insurance payment; not necessarily the insured.
entries.definitionCN: 接收保险赔付的人；不一定是 insured。

entries.definition: The one who owns and pays for the policy; usually also the insured.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并支付保单的人；通常也是 insured。

entries.definition: Any person or property covered; policyholder usually owns, insured is covered.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被保障的人或财产；policyholder 是拥有者，insured 是被保障者。

normal.en: insure + -ed past participle → insured = one who has been insured.
normal.cn: insure 加 -ed 过去分词 → insured = 被保险过的人。

normal.en: insured ↔ insurer: one is covered, the other covers.
normal.cn: insured ↔ insurer：一个被保障，一个去保障。

normal.en: insure ↔ ensure ↔ assure: all share sure, split into finance / certainty / reassurance.
normal.cn: insure ↔ ensure ↔ assure：都来自 sure，分成财务 / 确定 / 安慰。

normal.en: Compound opposites: insured vs uninsured, fully insured vs underinsured.
normal.cn: 复合反义词：insured vs uninsured，fully insured vs underinsured。

normal.en: Named insured vs additional insured on a policy.
normal.cn: 保单上的 named insured vs additional insured。

abstract.en: Picture a cloak that protects whoever wears it: insured = the wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件斗篷，谁穿上就保护谁；insured = 穿的人。

abstract.en: Picture a policy as a contract between insured and insurer, with coins in a pot between them.
abstract.cn: 想象保单是 insured 和 insurer 之间的合同，中间有一罐子硬币。

abstract.en: Picture the opposite: uninsured = standing out in the rain without an umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象对立面：uninsured = 没伞站在雨里。

examples.en: The insurer denied the claim because the insured had failed to disclose a prior condition.
examples.cn: 保险公司拒赔，因为被保险人未披露既往病史。

examples.en: Once the building was insured, the owner could relax a little about the fire risk.
examples.cn: 大楼一投保，业主对火灾风险就能松一口气。

examples.en: Self-insured employers set aside funds instead of buying a group health plan.
examples.cn: 自保的雇主自己留钱而不是购买团体健康险。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold: person covered → property covered → group under one policy → fully covered adjective → self-insured → named insured → additional insured → contrast with uninsured.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开：被保障的人 → 被保障的财产 → 一张保单下的群体 → fully 形容词 → 自保 → 指名被保险人 → 附加被保险人 → 与 uninsured 对比。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wearing a protective cloak labelled INSURED; coins are placed in the cloak pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人穿着标有 INSURED 的保护斗篷，口袋里放着硬币。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the insured party is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 人：被保险的当事人是核心名词义。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND GROUPS: insured covers objects too, and groups under one policy.
branches.cn: 财产与群体：insured 也指物，也指一张保单下的群体。

branches.en: THE ADJECTIVE STATE: fully covered.
branches.cn: 形容词状态：被充分覆盖的。

branches.en: SELF-INSURED: you yourself act as your own insurer.
branches.cn: 自保：你自己就是自己的 insurer。

branches.en: CONTRACTUAL ROLES AND CONTRAST: named, additional, and the opposite uninsured.
branches.cn: 合同角色与对比：指名、附加，以及反义词 uninsured。

intro.cn: insured = insure + -ed（过去分词）。insure = in- + sure。

items.exampleCN: 给车投保让司机变成 insured。

items.example: The participle becomes both adj. and noun.
items.exampleCN: 分词同时变成形容词和名词。

items.example: Insured means 'having been insured'.
items.exampleCN: Insured 意为「被保险过的」。

items.example: Ensure a door closes; insure a house.
items.exampleCN: Ensure 门要关好；insure 房子要保。

items.example: un- reverses insured.
items.exampleCN: un- 把 insured 反过来。

items.example: underinsured has less cover than needed.
items.exampleCN: underinsured 的保障不够用。

items.example: self- means the agent is yourself.
items.exampleCN: self- 表示行为人就是自己。

items.example: Less common than insured.
items.exampleCN: 没有 insured 常见。

items.exampleCN: insuree 是 insured 较少见的变体。

definition_zh: 保险费；溢价；额外费用；高等的
definition_en: the amount paid for insurance; an extra charge above a standard price; of the highest quality
core_image: 一张保单的顶部，放着一叠比普通钞票更厚更精致的钞票
scene: 小李在比较几份车险报价，最便宜的那份免赔额很高，贵一点的那份保费就贵了二十块。The monthly premium for the comprehensive policy was steep.
sceneCN: 这里 premium 指「保险费」（第 1 个义项：被保险人定期支付给保险人的金额）；句意为全保保单的月保费很高。图中可辨识物件：保单报价单、计算器、钞票。

pos.zh: 保险费（可数）；溢价（可数/不可数）
高等的；优质的

senses.title: insurance payment
senses.definition: a regular payment to an insurer in exchange for insurance cover
senses.definitionCN: 为换取保险保障而定期向保险人支付的金额
senses.example: She paid the premium once a year in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 她每年提前一次付清保费。
senses.why: This is the most common financial sense; the premium is what you 'pay for the prize' of cover.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的财务义；premium 就是你为保障的「奖赏」所付的钱。

senses.title: extra price above standard
senses.definition: an amount paid over and above the usual or base price
senses.definitionCN: 高于通常或基准价格的那部分金额
senses.example: You pay a premium for a seat with extra legroom.
senses.exampleCN: 腿部空间大的座位要多付钱。
senses.why: You pay more for something better, a 'prize' of better quality.
senses.whyCN: 更好的东西多付钱，一种更好质量的「奖赏」。

senses.title: reward or prize
senses.definition: an extra amount paid to encourage performance
senses.definitionCN: 为鼓励表现而额外支付的金额
senses.example: Workers got a premium for working the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 上夜班的工人有额外奖金。
senses.why: Premium was originally Latin for a reward or prize.
senses.whyCN: premium 原本在拉丁语里就是奖赏或奖品的意思。

senses.title: stock trading price above par
senses.definition: the amount a security trades above its face value
senses.definitionCN: 证券以高于其面值交易的金额
senses.example: The bond sold at a ten percent premium.
senses.exampleCN: 这支债券以高于面值百分之十的价格出售。
senses.why: When the market pays more than face value, that extra is the premium.
senses.whyCN: 市场支付的比面值高出来的那部分就是 premium。

senses.title: high quality adjective
senses.definition: of the highest quality or most expensive grade
senses.definitionCN: 最高质量或最贵等级的
senses.example: They stayed at a premium hotel near the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在机场附近的一家高档酒店。
senses.why: Adjective use from the 'best, extra' sense.
senses.whyCN: 来自「最好的、额外的」义的形容词用法。

senses.title: premium on your time
senses.definition: high value or importance placed on something scarce
senses.definitionCN: 给予稀缺事物的高价值或重要性
senses.example: In a startup, every minute is at a premium.
senses.exampleCN: 在创业公司里，每一分钟都很宝贵。
senses.why: Scarce things carry an extra price, so they are 'at a premium'.
senses.whyCN: 稀缺的东西都有额外价格，所以它们「at a premium」。

senses.title: options premium
senses.definition: the price paid for an options contract in finance
senses.definitionCN: 金融中为期权合同支付的价格
senses.example: The premium on the call option was three dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这支看涨期权的权利金是三美元。
senses.why: Another financial use: what you pay to buy the right to trade.
senses.whyCN: 另一种金融用法：你为购买交易权所付的钱。

senses.title: going premium
senses.definition: to become more valuable or scarce in demand
senses.definitionCN: 变得更值钱或更紧俏
senses.example: Rare stamps go premium when collectors bid for them.
senses.exampleCN: 稀有邮票在集邮者竞价时变得紧俏。
senses.why: The extra price you would pay shows how sought after it is.
senses.whyCN: 你愿意多付的那部分就说明它有多抢手。

intro.en: Premium comes from Latin praemium 'reward, prize'. The 'insurance payment' sense developed by analogy: you pay a small amount to get a big prize (compensation) if loss hits.
intro.cn: premium 来自拉丁语 praemium「奖赏、奖品」。保险费义是类比而来：你付一小笔钱，遭遇损失时就能获得一大笔「奖赏」（赔偿）。

items.en: Latin praemium meant 'reward, prize, money given as an incentive'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 praemium 意为「奖赏、奖品、作为激励的钱」。

items.en: Middle French premie 'reward' came from Latin praemium.
items.cn: 中古法语 premie「奖赏」来自拉丁语 praemium。

items.en: English borrowed premium around 1600 meaning 'reward, prize'.
items.cn: 英语约 1600 年借入 premium，意为「奖赏、奖品」。

items.en: The 'insurance payment' sense emerged by analogy with a prize around 1660, when early marine insurance spread.
items.cn: 保险费义约 1660 年通过与奖赏的类比出现，那时早期海上保险在发展。

items.en: The 'extra price' sense appeared in the 18th century; adjective use 'best quality' in the 19th.
items.cn: 「额外价格」义在 18 世纪出现；形容词「优质」义在 19 世纪。

items.en: Etymology solid; Latin praemium is well attested in inscriptions.
items.cn: 词源可靠；拉丁语 praemium 在铭文里有充分佐证。

note.en: Look-alikes are other -ium Latin nouns; near meanings are prices, rewards or charges.
note.cn: 形近是其他以 -ium 结尾的拉丁语名词；近义是价格、奖赏或收费。

entries.definition: Hatred; Latin odium 'hatred', unrelated to premium.
entries.definitionCN: 憎恨；来自拉丁语 odium，与 premium 无关。

entries.definition: A middle or a means; from Latin medius 'middle'.
entries.definitionCN: 中间或手段；来自拉丁语 medius「中间」。

entries.definition: Just shares the -ium ending; no root link.
entries.definitionCN: 只是共享 -ium 结尾，词根无关。

entries.definition: The root is praemium, not -ium alone.
entries.definitionCN: 词根是 praemium，不是单独的 -ium。

entries.definition: Any charge for a service; premium is specifically an insurance payment or extra price.
entries.definitionCN: 任何服务费；premium 特指保险费或额外价格。

entries.definition: An extra charge added to a base price.
entries.definitionCN: 加在基准价上的额外收费。

entries.definition: An extra payment for performance; premium is what you pay, bonus what you get.
entries.definitionCN: 因表现好而额外得到的钱；premium 是你付出去的，bonus 是你拿到的。

entries.definition: The premium in options trading is the price of the contract.
entries.definitionCN: 期权交易中的 premium 就是合同价格。

normal.en: premium ← Latin praemium 'reward, prize'.
normal.cn: premium ← 拉丁语 praemium「奖赏、奖品」。

normal.en: Insurance premium = small payment for a big reward (compensation) if luck runs out.
normal.cn: 保险费 = 花一小笔钱，运气不好时换一大笔「奖赏」（赔偿）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: pay a premium, at a premium, premium product.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：pay a premium 付保费、at a premium 溢价/紧俏、premium product 优质产品。

normal.en: Premium can be a noun or an adjective (premium class hotel).
normal.cn: premium 可以是名词也可以是形容词（premium 级的酒店）。

normal.en: At a premium means scarce or costing more.
normal.cn: at a premium 指紧俏或更贵。

abstract.en: Picture a small coin (premium) that buys you a giant shield (the insurance reward).
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小硬币（premium）换一面巨大的盾牌（保险奖赏）。

abstract.en: Picture Latin praemium: a prize cup filled with coins.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁语 praemium：一个装着硬币的奖杯。

abstract.en: Picture a scale: one side has the premium, the other has the coverage worth more.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平：一边是 premium，一边是更值钱的保障。

examples.en: The insurance premium rose every year as the risk of flooding became more obvious.
examples.cn: 随着洪水风险愈发明显，保险费年年上涨。

examples.en: Consumers willingly pay a premium for brands they trust.
examples.cn: 消费者愿意为自己信任的品牌多付钱。

examples.en: Premium class seats give passengers extra legroom and a wider meal menu.
examples.cn: 头等舱给乘客更大的腿部空间和更丰富的餐单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拉丁语 praemium = 奖赏 → 保险费是花钱买未来大奖赏 → premium

root: 拉丁语 praemium「奖赏、奖品」（prae-「前」+ emere「拿」，意为「先拿到的东西」）→ 中古法语 premie → 英语 premium。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from insurance payment → extra price → reward → stock above par → adjective high quality → scarce value → options premium → becoming tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从保险费 → 额外价格 → 奖赏 → 股票高于面值 → 形容词「优质」→ 稀缺价值 → 期权权利金 → 变得紧俏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small coin marked PREMIUM sits at the bottom of a giant shield.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚标着 PREMIUM 的小硬币坐在一面大盾牌底部。

branches.en: THE INSURANCE CORE: the most common financial use.
branches.cn: 保险核心：最常见的财务用法。

branches.en: THE COMMERCIAL EXTRA: anything you pay over the base price.
branches.cn: 商业额外费：任何超过基准价的支付。

branches.en: THE REWARD SENSE: going back to the Latin root.
branches.cn: 奖赏义：回到拉丁语词根。

branches.en: FINANCIAL MARKETS: bonds above par and options contracts.
branches.cn: 金融市场：高于面值的债券和期权合同。

branches.en: ADJECTIVE AND FIGURATIVE: high quality, scarce value, becoming tight.
branches.cn: 形容词与比喻：高质量、稀缺价值、变得紧俏。

intro.en: Premium comes from Latin praemium 'reward', possibly built on prae- + emere 'to take'.
intro.cn: premium 来自拉丁语 praemium「奖赏」，可能由 prae- + emere「拿」构成。

latinIntro.en: praemium = prae- 'before' + emere 'to take' (reconstructed but widely accepted).
latinIntro.cn: praemium = prae-「前」+ emere「拿」（构拟但被广泛接受）。

items.example: The root is a reward you take first.
items.exampleCN: 词根就是你先拿到的奖赏。

items.example: prae- puts you ahead in line.
items.exampleCN: prae- 让你排在前面。

items.example: Emere appears in emptor 'buyer' too.
items.exampleCN: Emere 也出现在 emptor「买家」里。

items.example: The word grew from reward to payment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从奖赏长到了付费。

items.example: preview, predict, prepare all use pre-.
items.exampleCN: preview、predict、prepare 都用 pre-。

items.example: An extra price is above the standard.
items.exampleCN: 额外价格就是在标准之上。

items.example: Latin emptor survives in caveat emptor 'buyer beware'.
items.exampleCN: Latin emptor 在 caveat emptor「买家注意」里留存。

items.example: Bonus and premium both name extra payments.
items.exampleCN: bonus 和 premium 都指额外支付。

items.example: Surcharge is always an add-on.
items.exampleCN: surcharge 总是一个附加。

items.example: Premium-priced goods cost more for being better.
items.exampleCN: Premium-priced 产品因更好而更贵。

definition_en: a legal or financial obligation to pay or do something; something that causes risk or difficulty
core_image: 一个人的脚上拴着一块大铁球，铁球上刻着「欠债必须还」，旁边摆着一份写着 liability 的表格
scene: 公司财务报表的右侧列着各种要付的钱：应付账款、长期借款、应计费用。Every liability on the balance sheet must be matched against an asset.
sceneCN: 这里 liability 指「公司负债」（第 2 个义项：公司财务上应支付的债务）；句意为资产负债表上总负债首次超过了总资产。图中可辨识物件：资产负债表、铁球、欠债数字。

pos.zh: 负债（可数/不可数）；责任（可数）

derivatives.zh: 联络（同拉丁词根但义不同）

senses.title: legal responsibility
senses.definition: a legal obligation to do or pay something
senses.definitionCN: 法律上做某事或付钱的义务
senses.example: The company denied all liability for the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认对事故负有任何法律责任。
senses.why: liable 'legally bound' + -ity makes the noun of the obligation.
senses.whyCN: liable「法律上有约束力的」+ -ity 就是这种义务的名词。

senses.title: financial debt or obligation
senses.definition: an amount owed in a company's or person's balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人资产负债表上所欠的金额
senses.example: Mortgages are long-term liabilities for households.
senses.exampleCN: 房贷是家庭的长期负债。
senses.why: A financial debt is a liability, something that binds you to pay.
senses.whyCN: 一笔财务债务就是 liability，绑着你去付钱。

senses.title: something that makes you liable
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes risk or exposure
senses.definitionCN: 带来风险或暴露的人或事
senses.example: His reckless driving made him a liability to the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他鲁莽的驾驶让他成了车队的负担。
senses.why: Something that can make you bound to pay is itself a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何能让你变得要出钱的东西本身就是 liability。

senses.title: tax or other duty
senses.definition: an amount due to a government or authority
senses.definitionCN: 欠政府或当局的金额
senses.example: Tax liabilities rise as profits grow.
senses.exampleCN: 利润增加，应纳税额也跟着上涨。
senses.why: Any amount you are bound to pay is a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何你必须付的金额都是 liability。

senses.title: limited liability
senses.definition: a legal structure where owners are only responsible for their investment
senses.definitionCN: 所有者仅对其投资负责的法律结构
senses.example: A limited liability company protects personal savings.
senses.exampleCN: 有限责任公司保护了个人的储蓄。
senses.why: The concept of liability is narrowed to protect owners.
senses.whyCN: liability 的概念被收窄来保护所有者。

senses.title: professional liability
senses.definition: legal responsibility of a professional for errors in work
senses.definitionCN: 专业人士对其工作失误的法律责任
senses.example: Doctors buy liability insurance for malpractice claims.
senses.exampleCN: 医生买职业责任险来应对医疗事故索赔。
senses.why: Professionals are bound to their clients for mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士对其客户的失误有约束力。

senses.title: contractual obligation
senses.definition: an obligation written into a contract between parties
senses.definitionCN: 合同中写明的各方之间的义务
senses.example: The liability to deliver expired when the contract terminated.
senses.exampleCN: 合同终止时，交货义务也过期了。
senses.why: Contracts create binding duties, which are liabilities.
senses.whyCN: 合同创造了有约束力的责任，就是 liabilities。

senses.title: environmental liability
senses.definition: legal obligation to clean up pollution or pay for harm
senses.definitionCN: 清理污染或赔偿损害的法律义务
senses.example: The old factory faces environmental liabilities from decades of waste.
senses.exampleCN: 老工厂因几十年的废弃物面临环境责任。
senses.why: A newer application of the general 'bound to pay' sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是「必须付钱」这个一般义的一个新应用。

intro.en: Liability comes from liable, which comes from Old French lier 'to bind'. Liability is the quality of being bound.
intro.cn: liability 来自 liable，后者来自古法语 lier「绑缚」。liability 就是「被绑着」的状态。

items.en: Latin ligare meant 'to bind'; it gave rise to liare, the Vulgar Latin for 'to bind, tie'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为「绑缚」，它产生了通俗拉丁语 liare「绑、系」。

items.en: Old French lier 'to bind, tie' came from Vulgar Latin liare.
items.cn: 古法语 lier「绑、系」来自通俗拉丁语 liare。

items.en: Middle English liabill meant 'legally bound, answerable'; it came from Old French lier.
items.cn: 中古英语 liabill 意为「法律上有约束力的、应负责的」，来自古法语 lier。

items.en: The suffix -ity (Latin -itas via French) turns the adjective liable into the noun liability.
items.cn: 后缀 -ity（拉丁语 -itas 经法语）把形容词 liable 变成名词 liability。

items.en: The balance-sheet sense 'debts owed' developed by the 17th century, as a debt binds you.
items.cn: 资产负债表上的「所欠债务」义在 17 世纪形成，因为债务就是绑着你的东西。

items.en: Etymology solid; ligare is well attested in classical Latin.
items.cn: 词源可靠；ligare 在古典拉丁语中有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the lig- bind root; near meanings are obligations or debts.
note.cn: 形近共享 lig-「绑」词根；近义是义务或债务。

entries.definition: Legally bound or responsible; liability is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上有约束力的或应负责的；liability 是它的名词。

entries.definition: A band of tissue that binds bones together.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨头绑在一起的一条组织。

entries.definition: To bind morally or legally; same lig- root.
entries.definitionCN: 在道德或法律上约束；同 lig- 词根。

entries.definition: To communicate and coordinate; from the same lier 'to bind'.
entries.definitionCN: 沟通协调；来自同一个 lier「绑」。

entries.definition: A specific sum owed; liability is broader and includes non-monetary obligations too.
entries.definitionCN: 所欠的一笔具体金额；liability 更宽，也包括非金钱义务。

entries.definition: A duty one is bound to perform; liability is specifically legal/financial.
entries.definitionCN: 被约束必须履行的义务；liability 特指法律/财务上的。

entries.definition: A general duty to act, not necessarily legal or financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的行动义务，不一定是法律或财务的。

entries.definition: In balance-sheet terms, exactly the debts side of the statement.
entries.definitionCN: 在资产负债表语境下，就是表中负债那一侧。

normal.en: Latin ligare 'to bind' → Old French lier → liable → liability.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare「绑缚」→ 古法语 lier → liable → liability。

normal.en: liable = bound; liability = the state of being bound.
normal.cn: liable = 被绑住的；liability = 被绑住的状态。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: total liabilities, financial liability, limited liability, liability insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：total liabilities 总负债、financial liability 财务负债、limited liability 有限责任、liability insurance 责任险。

normal.en: lig- root: ligament (body), oblige (duty), liaise (connect).
normal.cn: lig- 词根：ligament（身体里的韧带）、oblige（义务）、liaise（联络）。

normal.en: Balance sheet: assets = what you own, liabilities = what you owe.
normal.cn: 资产负债表：assets = 你拥有的，liabilities = 你欠下的。

abstract.en: Picture a man chained to a pile of coins that grows bigger every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被铁链拴在一堆每个月都在长大的硬币上。

abstract.en: Picture Latin ligare: ropes tying you to what you owe.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁语 ligare：绳子把你绑在你欠的东西上。

abstract.en: Picture a company's balance sheet as a seesaw: assets on one side, liabilities on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象公司的资产负债表是一架跷跷板：一边是资产，一边是负债。

examples.en: The startup took on significant liabilities to fund its rapid expansion.
examples.cn: 那家初创公司为快速扩张承担了大量负债。

examples.en: Owners of a limited liability company are not personally on the hook for its debts.
examples.cn: 有限责任公司的所有者不亲自替公司的债务背锅。

examples.en: The manufacturer faces product-liability claims from thousands of injured consumers.
examples.cn: 该制造商面临数千名受伤消费者的产品责任索赔。

dict_mnemonic.text: ligare（绑）→ liable（被绑的）→ liability = 绑着你的东西 → 负债/责任

root: 拉丁语 ligare「绑缚」→ 古法语 lier「绑」→ liable「被绑的」→ -ity 构成 liability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from legal responsibility → financial debt → risky person/thing → taxes → limited liability → professional duty → contract duty → environmental duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开：法律责任 → 财务债务 → 风险人/事 → 税款 → 有限责任 → 职业义务 → 合同义务 → 环境义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person chained to a growing pile of coins labelled LIABILITIES.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被铁链拴在一写着 LIABILITIES、越来越大的硬币堆上。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CORE: being bound by law.
branches.cn: 法律核心：被法律绑着。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL USE: debts on the balance sheet.
branches.cn: 财务用法：资产负债表上的债务。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT USE: a person or thing that causes risk.
branches.cn: 抽象用法：带来风险的人或事。

branches.en: PUBLIC DUTY: taxes and government charges.
branches.cn: 公共义务：税款和政府收费。

branches.en: SPECIALISED FORMS: limited liability, professional, contract, environmental.
branches.cn: 专业形式：有限责任、职业、合同、环境责任。

intro.en: Liability = liable + -ity; liable ← Old French lier ← Latin ligare 'to bind'.
intro.cn: liability = liable + -ity；liable ← 法 lier ← 拉丁 ligare「绑缚」。

latinIntro.en: ligare = to bind. The whole word family shares this core.
latinIntro.cn: ligare = 绑缚。整个家族都共享这个核心。

items.example: The root means to physically tie things together.
items.exampleCN: 词根就是把东西绑在一起。

items.example: Old French took ligare into Romance.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把 ligare 带入罗曼语。

items.example: liable means 'can be bound'.
items.exampleCN: liable 意为「能被绑住的」。

items.example: -ity turns the adjective into the noun of state.
items.exampleCN: -ity 把形容词变成表状态的名词。

items.example: Possibility, reality, liability all use -ity.
items.exampleCN: possibility、reality、liability 都用 -ity。

items.example: Same lig- root in anatomy.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学里也用同一个 lig- 词根。

items.example: Oblige uses ob- 'toward' the binding.
items.exampleCN: Oblige 用 ob-「朝向」绑着。

items.example: Liaison originally meant a binding link between parties.
items.exampleCN: Liaison 原意为各方之间的绑着的联系。

items.example: Religion also traces to ligare via religare.
items.exampleCN: Religion 也通过 religare 追溯到 ligare。

items.example: Obligation and liability are close neighbours.
items.exampleCN: Obligation 和 liability 是近邻。

definition_zh: 资产；财产；优点；有用的东西
definition_en: something of value owned by a person or company; a useful or valuable quality or person
core_image: 一个宝箱打开着，里面闪闪发光的金币、金条和珠宝，每一件都贴着写着 dollar value 的标签
scene: 家庭会计表格的左栏列着房子、车子、存款和股票，右栏列着房贷和信用卡欠款。A house is the largest single asset on most household balance sheets.
sceneCN: 这里 asset 指「公司/个人的财务资产」（第 2 个义项：资产负债表上由主体拥有的有价值项目）；句意为银行估价她的总资产超过两百万美元。图中可辨识物件：资产负债表、宝箱、钞票。

pos.zh: 资产（可数；复数最常用）；优点（可数）

senses.title: something valuable owned
senses.definition: any item of value owned by a person, company or institution
senses.definitionCN: 个人、公司或机构拥有的任何有价值物品
senses.example: Her main asset was a portfolio of blue-chip stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要资产是一篮子蓝筹股。
senses.why: The word came through Norman French from Latin ad sedem 'settled', meaning property.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经诺曼法语来自拉丁语 ad sedem「坐定的」，指财产。

senses.title: balance-sheet item
senses.definition: a line on the left side of a balance sheet representing value held
senses.definitionCN: 资产负债表左侧的一行，代表持有的价值
senses.example: Total assets must equal total liabilities plus equity.
senses.exampleCN: 总资产必须等于总负债加股东权益。
senses.why: The accounting convention puts all assets on one side.
senses.whyCN: 会计惯例把所有资产放在一侧。

senses.title: financial asset
senses.definition: money or a claim to money, such as cash, bonds or shares
senses.definitionCN: 金钱或对金钱的索取权，如现金、债券、股票
senses.example: Banks create financial assets when they make loans.
senses.exampleCN: 银行放贷时就创造了金融资产。
senses.why: A sub-type of asset: assets that are financial claims.
senses.whyCN: asset 的一个子类型：财务上的索取权。

senses.title: tangible asset
senses.definition: a physical thing of value, such as property or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 有实物形态的有价值之物，如房产或设备
senses.example: The factory is the company's largest tangible asset.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂是公司最大的有形资产。
senses.why: A physical sub-type; its opposite is intangible.
senses.whyCN: 有形的子类型；反义词是 intangible。

senses.title: intangible asset
senses.definition: a non-physical asset such as a brand, patent or goodwill
senses.definitionCN: 非实物的资产，如品牌、专利、商誉
senses.example: The brand is more valuable than the factory on the books.

senses.title: useful quality
senses.definition: a skill or quality that is valuable in a role
senses.definitionCN: 在一个职位上有价值的技能或品质
senses.example: Her organisational skills are a real asset to the team.

senses.why: Figurative extension: a quality that works for you is an asset.

senses.title: valuable person

senses.example: The senior engineer is the team's greatest asset.

senses.title: asset in law

senses.definitionCN: 破产中可用来还债的财产

intro.en: Asset comes from Old French aset, a shortened phrase from the Latin ad sedem meaning 'to the seat, settled', referring to property you could count on.
intro.cn: asset 来自古法语 aset，是拉丁语短语 ad sedem「到座位上、坐定的」的简写，指你能指望得上的财产。

items.en: Latin ad sedem = ad 'to' + sedem 'seat' (accusative of sedes). Literally 'to the seat', figuratively 'settled, established'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad sedem = ad「到」+ sedem「座位」（sedes 的宾格）。字面「到座位上」，比喻「坐定的、确立的」。

items.en: Vulgar Latin assetum developed as a noun from the phrase, meaning 'property settled on a person'.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 assetum 从这个短语变成名词，意为「安在某人名下的财产」。

items.en: Old French aset appeared in the 12th century meaning 'property, goods'.
items.cn: 古法语 aset 在 12 世纪出现，意为「财产、财物」。

items.en: English borrowed asset in the 14th century, first meaning 'sufficient property to meet obligations'.
items.cn: 英语 14 世纪借入 asset，最初意为「足以履行义务的财产」。

items.en: The accounting sense 'balance-sheet item' developed by the 18th century; the figurative 'useful quality' in the 19th.
items.cn: 资产负债表义在 18 世纪形成；比喻「有用品质」义在 19 世纪。

items.en: Etymology solid; the ad sedem origin was first proposed in the 19th century and is now standard.
items.cn: 词源可靠；ad sedem 的起源在 19 世纪首次提出，现在已成为标准说法。

note.en: Look-alikes share no root (it's a unique borrowing); near meanings are related to things of value.
note.cn: 形近词没有共同词根（它是独特借词）；近义围绕有价值之物展开。

definition_en: a non-physical asset that represents a claim to future cash flows, such as cash, bonds, shares or derivatives

senses.title: claim to cash flows
senses.definition: a non-physical contract or instrument that gives its holder a right to future payments
senses.definitionCN: 赋予持有者未来收取款项权利的非实物合约或工具
senses.example: Stocks and bonds are both financial assets.
senses.exampleCN: 股票和债券都是金融资产。
senses.why: A sub-type of asset, distinguished by being a claim rather than a physical thing.
senses.whyCN: asset 的一个子类型，特点是索取权而不是实物。

senses.title: cash and equivalents
senses.definition: cash on hand, bank deposits and short-term highly liquid instruments
senses.definitionCN: 手头的现金、银行存款和短期高流动性工具
senses.example: The company kept financial assets in short-term government debt.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把金融资产放在短期政府债里。
senses.why: Cash itself is a financial asset, the most liquid kind.
senses.whyCN: 现金本身就是金融资产，流动性最高的那类。

senses.title: loans as bank assets
senses.definition: loans made by a bank, which are assets on its balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 银行发放的贷款，在其资产负债表上是资产
senses.example: Mortgages are the largest class of bank financial assets.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押贷款是银行金融资产的最大类。
senses.why: When a bank lends, it creates a financial asset for itself.
senses.whyCN: 银行放款时就为自己创造了一项金融资产。

senses.title: derivative instruments
senses.definition: options, futures, swaps and other instruments whose value derives from another asset
senses.definitionCN: 期权、期货、互换等价值来自其他资产的工具
senses.example: Derivatives can grow into huge financial assets or liabilities.
senses.exampleCN: 衍生品可以膨胀成巨额金融资产或负债。
senses.why: Even synthetic claims count as financial assets.
senses.whyCN: 即使是合成的索取权也算金融资产。

senses.title: securitised assets
senses.definition: a pool of loans packaged into tradeable securities
senses.definitionCN: 打包成可交易证券的一揽子贷款
senses.example: Mortgage-backed securities are bundled financial assets.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押贷款支持证券就是打包后的金融资产。
senses.why: Repackaging loans into securities makes them tradeable financial assets.
senses.whyCN: 把贷款打包成证券就变成了可交易的金融资产。

senses.title: foreign currency holdings
senses.definition: cash or deposits in a foreign currency held by a person or country
senses.definitionCN: 个人或国家持有的外币现金或存款
senses.example: Central banks hold large financial assets in foreign currencies.
senses.exampleCN: 央行持有大量外币金融资产。
senses.why: Any currency you hold is a financial asset, foreign or domestic.
senses.whyCN: 你持有的任何货币都是金融资产，不管是外币还是本币。

senses.title: intellectual property as finance
senses.titleCN: 作为金融资产的知识产权
senses.definition: patents, trademarks and copyrights bought and sold for financial return
senses.definitionCN: 为财务回报而买卖的专利、商标、版权
senses.example: Some firms treat patents as their core financial asset.
senses.exampleCN: 有些公司把专利视为核心金融资产。
senses.why: Intangible claims treated financially count as financial assets.
senses.whyCN: 被以财务方式对待的无形资产也算金融资产。

senses.title: employee stock options
senses.definition: options given to employees as part of compensation
senses.definitionCN: 作为薪酬一部分给员工的期权
senses.example: Options became a significant financial asset for senior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 期权成了高管的一项重要金融资产。
senses.why: Employee options are derivative financial assets in the employee's hands.
senses.whyCN: 员工期权在员工手里就是衍生金融资产。

intro.en: Financial asset is a compound of financial (from Latin finis 'end, boundary') and asset (from Latin ad sedem 'to the seat').
intro.cn: financial asset 是 financial（来自拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」）和 asset（来自拉丁语 ad sedem「到座位上」）的复合。

items.en: Latin finis 'end, boundary' became Old French fin and then finance 'payment of a debt'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」变成古法语 fin，再变成 finance「债务的支付」。

items.en: English finance borrowed from Old French around 1400, first meaning 'a payment to settle a debt'.
items.cn: 英语 finance 约 1400 年从古法语借入，最初意为「结清债务的一笔付款」。

items.en: Asset comes from Vulgar Latin assetum, from the Latin phrase ad sedem 'settled property'.
items.cn: asset 来自通俗拉丁语 assetum，后者来自拉丁语短语 ad sedem「坐定的财产」。

items.en: financial asset as a technical term in finance appears in early 20th-century textbooks and bank regulations.
items.cn: financial asset 作为金融术语出现于 20 世纪初的教材和银行监管中。

items.en: The International Accounting Standards Board now has a formal definition: a contract that gives one party a financial asset and the other a financial liability.
items.cn: 国际会计准则理事会现在有正式定义：一种合同，给一方金融资产，给另一方金融负债。

items.en: Both words have solid etymology; the compound is modern and technical.
items.cn: 两个词的词源都可靠；复合词是现代技术用语。

note.en: Look-alikes share the asset root; near meanings are neighbouring classes of asset.
note.cn: 形近共享 asset 词根；近义是邻近的资产类别。
